review: Worth a try!. This kit is a great deal!  I've been a devoted user of Korean skin care products.  For a while, I have preferred, out of several brands and types of sheet mask, the Benton Bee and Snail sheet mask.  Fantastic product!!!!  Firms, smooths, soothes.  It's great.  However, that's not why I purchased this set.  I have combo skin that leans towards oily in the heat.  Super oily T-zone.  After doing a ton of research, I decided to give the Benton Aloe Gel moisturizer a try.  I'd also heard great things about this foam cleanser.  I'm really enjoying the cleanser so far.  I wet my hands and face, use only a pea sized amount, rub my hands together to create the foam (not a soapy lather, but a thick and creamy foam), and work over my face.  I do this after oil cleansing.  This does a great job of picking up any oil residue and dirt, while leaving my face soft and refreshed.  Never tight and dry, which is the sign of an awful cleanser.  The gel moisturizer is okay.  Just okay.  I don't get as oily as I did with lotion moisturizers, which is great.  However, I don't have that supple, smooth feel that I'm used to and prefer.  I've actually noticed flaking around my nose, which is something I never dealt with after moisturizing.  A pea sized amount covers my entire face, it leaves a slightly tacky finish until absorbed ( I always let each of my products absorb for around 90 seconds before applying the next step), and is completely colorless.  Will I repurchase?  No, but I do suggest that you give this a try if your research and needs point you this direction.  Everyone's skin care needs can vary on several levels.  There are universal musts for good skin health, like cleansing daily, moisturizing, and using a good sunscreen.  There a a ton a variations of those products, though.  Finding the right routine and products can be a trial and error process.  The main thing is to stick to it.  The results are worth it!

review: Halloween Or Messing Around Okay, But Serious Wear, Not So Much. I have been working with wigs for quite a few years now.  One thing I know is a good quality vs not so great quality wig.  Let's take a look at this one.  WHAT IS THIS LIKE?  HAIR This wig has some great hair. the colors are definitely platinum white and what I would call light auburn base hairs.  The white hairs are about 1/3 or so longer than the auburn hairs.  There is a nice kink to the hairs.  THICKNESS That is where this wig is sadly lacking.  At the top, the wefts of hair are way too far apart. The lace in the cap is a very light butter colored yellow.  The hair is not too thin, but it is not quite thick enough to cover hair below.  Yes, this comes with a nylon cap, but it just is not comfortable with those.  If you have dark hair it will definitely show the bright colored lace and elastics through the wig when the wind blows.  BANGS/STYLE That is where this wig is just not practical unless you don't mind looking stupid for a party or Halloween.  The bangs are WAY too long for anyone to wear.  That usually would not be a problem, but what you will get instead of the cool light ends on the entire head is chopped bang that is bland looking and then these white cool looking ends around the head.  The bangs are best cut painstakingly so that the auburn is cut way shorter (about 2/3) than the white hairs.  That takes a lot of time but worth the effort.  Then you have to cut them at a staggered manner.  Other than the bangs being hard to trim so you can at least function with this wig on, the overall style is fabulous.  I love how it falls and looks while on the head.  ELASTIC BANDS Inside the wig, there are elastic bands with hooks to help hold the wig on the head. You might want to take them down to the spot you like it in as the hooks have a tendency to come undone during wearing.  WHAT I WANT IN A WIG Believe it or not, I would actually wear a wig like this with the right outfit, and not to be silly either.  I prefer wigs that look authentic,, and can be worn realistically as well as for fun.  1.  I have to be able to see out of it 2.  I have to be able to wear it comfortably without fussing 3.  I want it to not have my real hair showing 4.  I want it to look realistic 5.  I want it to last for quite a few wearings  DOES THIS WIG PASS THE TEST? I am giving this wig THREE stars because it is hard to wear and see.  In order to trim this in a realistic manner, I have to take a LOT of time and that takes stars off for me.  I happen to love the style and coloring, so I am wiling to put the work into it, but honestly, I think it should be a bit shorter in the bangs area since it is so hard to trim and keep it looking real.  Also, the wefting on the top is just a bit too widely spaced.  I wish also that the cap was made with light auburn lace and elastic instead of the icy yellow colors.  THE BOTTOM LINE If you want to wear this for fun, it will be hard to see and hard to trim and not look silly in this.  It is comfortable and the style is epic, but there will be work required.  You can bandana it to help, but it still will look a bit floppy unless trimmed a little bit in the bangs/fringe area.  I like this, but it takes work to wear and not look silly for me.  MY RATING THREE STARS.  The trimming of the bangs is VERY time consuming since we only have one shot at it and if it is screwed up, then the wig is toast.  I wish there was more hair on top and that the lace cap did not show as easily.  A darker cap underneath (light auburn color) would have been much nicer with this.  I will still use this, but it could have been a bit nicer with small inexpensive changes

review: Try it, it's kind of awesome!. I have white skin. Like, white white.My arms and face generally see a little sun in the summer and darken slightly, but I take care to wear SPF so I never see much change. My legs, on the other hand, are a problem. White. Blinding.Horrifying. I've tried many self tanning products in the past, mostly lotions and foams. They all worked okay, usually with streaking and the dreaded orange tone, but what is a girl to expect? I can tell you now, there's more out there for us than orange legs. This yea is the first in 3 or 4 that I have actually chosen to wear shorts. I figured, I'm too old to care what people think about my stretch marks, white legs, weird veins. So I bought a Loreal spray bronzer a few weeks ago. I was left with horribly streaky legs that I had no choice but to cover up. I can deal with my own legs, but streaked legs? I couldn't do it. I found this Bronze Doll spray and I decided to give it a try. I've never used a mitt before and I was curious. I waited until the streaking from the last tanner I tried was completely gone before using this, because I wanted to give it a fair shot. Immedietely upon spraying the product into the mitt and rubbing it on my legs, they were transformed. I can't lie, it looked like I was spreading paint on my chunky white calves. It was almost a purple color. I was shocked, but I kept going. I rubbed the product onto both legs, being as careful as I could. It had a really pleasant scent, almost tropical, but it went away when the product dried. Dry time was about a minute- but I didn't put my shorts on for a few minutes after that. I didn't notice any transfer whatsoever, either on my clothing or my white bed sheets. By the time I went to bed, the color had settled to a nice bronze. Not too dark, but very noticeable. My legs ended up a little splotchy, but I know that it was due to user error. I woke up with nicely tanned legs, for the first time in years. Then I took a shower. As soon as the water hit my legs, it turned brown. I can honestly say, I wasn't expecting that. I rubbed my legs a little and no additional product seemed to come off. When I got out of the shower, I saw that the color had been reduced by about half, but was still obvious on my skin.I will reapply tonight to help with some of my mistakes from yesterday. This is a dark enough product that I think I can only use it 3 times a week if I want to look normal, and I pretty much do. I love the way it makes my skin look. I love the way it makes my calves (my most hated body part) look! I can't say that I will try it on other parts of my body, but I will being using it throughout the summer on my legs.The mitt makes an obvious (for me) difference in ease and quality of application. I am very happy with this, and I will repurchase it if I run out before September, (which is when I will most likely go back to covering up all the time). I was able to purchase this product at a reduced cost in exchange for an honest review. All opinions are my own. When I repurchase the product, I will happily do so at full cost

review: It' Pretty Good. Saw this puppy discussed a lot on various shaving sites. They all said that you have to watch the YouTube videos to get the right technique for lathering. I watched a couple and have been trying this now for the past several weeks. I must have tried close to 40 different soaps, creams and sticks from the most expensive to the not so expensive. This one is right up there in terms of face glide and lubrication.Certainly in the top quintile. Why 4 stars? I have tried every variation to get a lather but there is no getting around that this is the most difficult soap I have ever tried. Too much water, too little water it seemed impossible to get it right the first time. No matter what I tried it seemed to either be too foamy and thin or not enough water to generate a lather. It's as if the gremlin in the soap puck was contrary enough to defeat whatever I tried until the 2nd or 3rd try. Bottom lime- With effort and persistence it gets the job done and the fragrance is mildly pleasant but it will never be my "go-to" product. I'll stick with may favs: Kiss My Face, Cella and Proraso cream. UPDATE: Gave it another try with a little more patience. It seems that the end product you want is a little on the thick creamy side and not really a "lather". If you wet your brush, turn it over and let all the water drip out that you can,then you apply brush to soap and be patient and determined you will get the thick rich cream that will do the trick. One other tip I found after you apply the cream to the face let it sit for about 20-30 seconds before you apply your razor. You will then get the greatest glide you will experience. Accordingly I have moved it up the top tier and displaced the Proraso cream.I would give it 4 1/2 stars, and not 5, if I could because of the difficult lathering. FURTHER UPDATE After using this puppy for a little while I have come to master it and love it. Great for glide and closeness and absence of irritation. I originally rated it a 4 but now after careful consideration I must admit that it deserves a 5 star rating. Its among my top 3 favorite shaving products

It is a gentler alternative to retinol, which is perfect for someone like me because I have sensitive skin.  This Korean beauty product arrived nicely packaged. From the outside of the jar, I thought this cream was a pale yellow, but it’s actually white. I used a small dollop and it was enough to cover my entire face and neck area too. The texture is light and creamy. There is no scent and it goes on clear after gently rubbing it in. I have combination to oily, sensitive skin and this did not feel greasy or make my face breakout, which is a huge plus!  I’ve been using this Bakuchiol cream in combination with a hyaluronic acid serum for only one week and the results are just AMAZING! My skin looks brighter and hydrated, and feels so nice and supple! Although I haven’t seen my wrinkles improve yet, I will happily continue using this product because the results so far have been very positive and promising! You  dear Bakuchiol cream have earned a coveted spot on my limited bathroom counter space!

review: Follain  Does What It Promises To Do. You know the saying 'kill two birds with one stone'? That is precisely what I had in mind when I ordered Follain Mattifying Moisturizer.  I have dry, sensitive skin but its not oily. My husband has oily skin. I have fine lines and wrinkles on my face. My husband does not.  Because Follain moisturizer promises to combat oily skin, as well as fine lines and wrinkles and is a clean, vegan product, I ordered it to find out if it could help the both of us with our skin issues.  I'm happy to tell you that it has helped the both of us.  The moisturizer is a bit thinner than I'm used to. I don't say that in a bad way because its not at all bad.  One pump of the canister delivers enough moisturizer to cover my facial skin. Its very lightweight and absorbs quickly without leaving a look or feel of oily/greasy skin. It provides immediate hydration and does a nice job of softening my skin. I am VERY happy to say I absolutely have a noticeable reduction in the fine lines and wrinkles on my face. They don't go away entirely, but there is a definite reduction in size and appearance. ( I can't tell you how much I needed to experience this right now as my 49th bday is this week...that means 5-0 isn't far behind and I'm kind of starting to freak about it! )  My husband also tried this for his oily skin with impressive results.  Follain controls his oily skin and prevents the shiny, damp look that comes with oily skin thanks to the mattifying benefit of this moisturizer. review: Norelco 1050cc vs. Braun Pulsonic 9595. I bought the new Philips Norelco 1050cc Arcitec Shaving System, returned it for a refund after 30 days, and then purchased a the new Braun Pulsonic 9595 Shaving System. Since I've had experience with both now, I thought my experience might be of value to others. I've had 3 Norelco shavers over the past 20 years. The 9595 is my first Braun shaver.  Shaving Closeness - The Braun definitely gives a closer shave and in less time, although the Norelco is acceptable. One reviewer commented about getting nicks from the Braun but I have not had that problem at all, even around the chin.  Comfort - The Braun feels heavier (I didn't actually weigh them) but I found the Braun more comfortable to hold.  Noise - The Braun is noisier, especially during the cleaning cycle.  Status Indicators on the Shaver - The indicators are better on the Braun; however, I've since learned that's mostly because I had the 1050 model. I now see that the 1060 or the 1090 models would have been better and probably would equal the Braun.  Charging/Cleaning Stand - The Braun is more convenient to replace the cleaning fluid but about the same cost (about $1.00 per week). Both seem to clean equally well. The charge and cleaning status lights on the Braun are easier to see and give better status information. But the big difference here is the way the charging system works. With the Braun, you simply place your used razor in the stand, push a button, and the cleaning & charging are taken care of. However, with the Norelco, there are a number of warnings in the book to unplug the unit after it completes its cycle. This is a major inconvenience if you have to hang around and remember to unplug the unit. Also, the lack of an on/off switch seems a poor and cheap design.  Trimmer - To even off my sideburns, I found the Norelco somewhat difficult to use because the trimmer did not stick out far enough beyond the shaving head. This was not a problem with the Braun.  Cost - The Braun cost about $20 more.  Return Policy - 60 day money back with Norelco; only 30 days with Braun.  Bottom-Line - I started with a bias toward the Norelco because of my past experiences but in my opinion, this new Braun definitely surpasses the Norelco in terms of shaving closeness and convenience. Braun is clearly worth the extra $20, although the Norelco is a decent product

In my opinion, this scent best suits a feminine individual with grace and compassion. But she still has that boost of confidence to her, she knows her place yet she remains humble and kind.  I would best pair this scent with someone like Solji from EXID (a Korean pop group). Who's quite feminine and sweet but has powerful and gorgeous vocals. review: LumaRx facial cleaning brush is like a Sonicare ElectricToothbrush for the face. After moistening my face and the brush heads with water, I tested the sensitive and normal heads with both soap and [[ASIN:B01648QDS4 L'Oreal Paris Age Perfect Facial Cream Cleanser, 5 Fluid Ounce]] and the massaging head with water alone. After a one-minute "application" with any one of the brushes, I love how smooth and clean this makes my face feel.  The packages includes:  - three brush heads (sensitive, normal, and massage) and their covers which have air vents to hasten drying - one charging base with power cord - one brush wand that operates at 3 speed levels - one white plastic zippered travel case - one instruction pamphlet  PROS:  - The wand contains a rechargeable battery that last for 30 uses. The first charge takes up to six hours.  It also has a 30 minute fast-charge feature that will provide 4-5 uses. By the way, I love the charging light on the base; it has a "cool" factor to it.  - There's a one minute timer that has what I call a "tripacer" (like Sonicare's quadpacer) timer built in for each of the three zones of the face. These zones are the T zone, left side, and right side. What this means is that the unit pauses ever so slightly ever twenty seconds to let the user know when it's time to move on to the next zone so that the cleaning time can be distributed evenly among zones.  - None of the three brushes were rough or extremely abrasive. The rotating and vibrating brush heads were as gentle as could be and I have sensitive skin.  - The wand with brush can be used in the shower as long as it's not fully submerged in water.  - This can be used to remove cosmetics.  - The unit comes with a 2-year limited warranty.  CONS:  - Although these brushes remove make-up effectively, I personally only like to use this on the days I do not wear makeup. The reason is that the eye area has to be avoided. I use eye makeup so I wind up washing my entire face with my hands instead as it does not make sense to me to use a brush on only part of my face.  - There are a lot of don'ts in the manual like don't submerge in water, don't use around the eyes, don't use if you are taking steroid-based medication, don't operate outdoors or where there are aerosol products or oxygen being administered, etc.  - If used daily at no more than the maximum two times per day, the brush heads need to be replaced  every three months. The Massaging head (since it doesn't not have bristles) can be replaced every six months. This can get expensive. I contacted the company for the replacement price and they said they would let me know when it's orderable on Amazon. I will update the comments section of this review with that information when I receive it.  - The battery on this unit is NOT replaceable as per the email from them which I posted in the comments section of this review.  At first I questioned why would I need such a facial cleansing tool. After using this, however, I realized that I love how it makes my face feel so clean and smooth. This is not a tool I would use more than twice per week since I really hate using this to remove makeup, however, it's so gentle on my skin that I look forward to the cleansing action, mildly exfoliating properties, and the light massage it provides me all without the use of a chemical masque

review: it's ok but I would not recommend it. It was tough to decide whether or not to give this product one or two stars, but I gave it two because it doesn't completely suck, it's just not as good as other razors that aren't as expensive The manufacturer recommends waiting 21 days before deciding to keep this product or send it back. I would also give the same recommendation to people who are looking at purchasing this. I bought it because I needed to replace my old razor. My old Remington titanium R9710 was a good razor but it ripped the hair out of my neck area and left me with very irritated skin. The thing about my old razor is that it had floating heads and it handled long hairs pretty well if I was lazy and didn't shave. This new Arcitec worked very well when I first got it but I really wanted to try it out and only had stubble on my face at the time. It worked very well with short hairs and left me with no irritated skin on my neck.  Well I wanted to see what it would act like if I let my hair grow a little and it did not perform like I thought it would. It took a long time to shave and I had to go over the area multiple times in multiple directions and with different pressures just to get a few long hairs. This new head style has really been a downgrade because when you apply pressure, the heads seem to pull away from your face on the outside part of it and it makes it harder to shave. It was either that or the fact that it doesn't have a hair collection area. It fills up with hair rather quickly so maybe that has an impact on how well it shaves. Cleaning the unit was very simple but I think I would have the cleaning system of one of the speed XL models over this. You have to pop open three separate chambers rather than flip the whole head up to clean each blade. A nice feature of this razor is the tube trimmer. You can take the razor head right off and pop out the trimmer. There really isn't much else to say about the trimmer other than I thought it worked great.  Overall, this is a very nice looking razor, but the functionality of the razor itself is pretty bad. It does come with a nice travel case and charging stand as well. The travel case is made of hard plastic and does not have room for the charger, but it does have the capability to charge the razor, so you do not need to bring along the charging stand. If you want to try this product I would say go for it because Norelco has such a generous return policy and maybe you will like it better than I did. If you think you like the functions of this razor but really aren't sure about it, I would not recommend it because it doesn't work like I think a razor should (it takes a long time to shave and it doesn't work well on longer hairs). review: Nothing spectacular. I have received more... for this price.. This Hair Removal Device by Ulike just as well as a couple of other IPL devices I have that cost much less. It comes packaged nicely, though I kept trying to open the flat two-sided green piece that covers the accessory side. It doesn't open. The device does look quite fancy, and I was interested in skin rejuvenation, which is in one of the photos (that is mentioned in the other listing that shows this exact same device). The instruction booklet contains about as much as the empty listing page that I ordered it from. That page has no bullet points, only one photo. They do have another listing for this same exact device, showing the accessories, extra photos with bits of information, and bullet points telling a little about it. I got my information from there. The device does have the cooling feature, as many others do, which helps it not to zap too badly. It also comes with a razor and eye protection. What it lacks, that many others include that are in or around this price range, is more attachments for the device. There needs to be at least one smaller light head for use around the lip area, as it's very hard to use the main one with the device being so large. This IPL device works pretty much as well as any other, with none having the ability to make you completely hair-free at any point in the future. As far as the studies that I have seen, with diligent use, home IPL devices can only offer a little better than 50-60%-ish less hair. My preferred device, which costs very little more than this one, has several attachments, including some specifically for skin rejuvenation. You do get a fancy box with this device, and it looks nice, but I don't think it provides any more or less than devices that cost much less. I haven't found one yet that really only takes 10 minutes to do your legs, but if I ever do, that is the one that would probably take the cake! If you like fancy boxes and a sleek-looking device, I would recommend this one

review: Vague Label Ingredients, But Lathers Well, Smells Good. I am pretty picky when it comes to my body washes. I like one that has good ingredients, and a great smell. When I saw the label for this saying Argan Oil, Coconut Oil and Tea Tree Oil, I knew it would be right up my alley. I love all 3 of those ingredients and they work well with my skin. I was excited to use this. When it arrived and I checked the ingredients label, I was shocked. Like so many other reviews, I don't see any of the above listed on the label. Some ingredients are very vague. Some of the ingredients I had never heard of before and had to look up. My suggestion to the company is to make the label a bit more descriptive and clearly put what is inside. What essences? What type of vegetable oils? Since it is so unclear, if you have easily irritated or sensitive skin I would stay away from this. The vague label makes it hard to use by anyone who may have allergies to certain things.  On the other hand, I will say that I do like the body wash. It smells fantastic, like a herbal scent. It lathers nicely and feels good on the skin. Doesn't dry my skin out.  If the label was changed and I knew exactly what was in this I would easily bump this up to a 5 star rating. But because I have no clue what is inside this, I have to bump it down.  *Please note that I was sent this product either complimentary or discounted in order to provide my honest experience, thoughts and review

review: BURNS LIKE POISON. At first, I was skeptical of this product because it had no preservatives. Normally, no preservatives is good, but as anyone who's ever tried to make their own clay masks should know, clay/mud and water are notorious for being difficult to preserve "naturally" since it is highly susceptible to bacterial and fungal (mold) growth. Despite this, I bought the product because I wanted a cheap product to tide me over while I waited on materials to mix my own batch.  When I first opened the package, I immediately noticed a strong metallic smell, almost chemical in nature. I figured it COULD be some kind of metal found in the dirt, so I proceeded, though wary. I washed my face with a mild and gentle cleanser, patted it dry, mixed up the mask, and proceeded to use the brush to apply it onto my face. IMMEDIATELY, it started to burn. It burned like NOTHING I had felt before, and I regularly use AHA/BHA acids to chemically exfoliate & tone. I double checked the ingredients, and there is ABSOLUTELY NOTHING in the mask that should make it burn that way. I began to wash off the mask, but the burning sensation increased EXPONENTIALLY as I splashed water on my face to wash off the thin layer of mask that I had applied.  I can only guess that the burning is from one of two things: 1) the manufacturer lied about the ingredients or 2) the quality of the product was compromised by the fact that there were no preservatives, allowing harmful bacteria or fungus to manifest. I should note that there was no visible mold, but the fact is that you cannot determine with absolute certainty the presence or lack of bacteria/fungi in a product unless you do a microbial test, which I do not have handy.  I cannot say anything except that I would STRONGLY ADVISE AGAINST BUYING THIS MASK or any masks with similar ingredients

review: Much better then the Sonic Spinbrush by Arm & Hammer. Until a year ago, I never liked the idea of owning an electric toothbrush: I'd owned several cheap ones and never liked any of them. Then I figured that I'd try one again about a year ago and so I chose the Sonic Spinbrush by Arm & Hammer. I chose the Spinbrush because it had a large brush, which I thought meant less time/effort brushing my teeth.  The Spinbrush worked pretty well, but the large brush head gagged me horribly. Because of this, I decided to give the Oral-B Vitality a try and I like it much better. The first reason I prefer the Vitality is because it has a much smaller brush head (you don't need a large brush with an electric toothbrush, since the toothbrush is doing all the work.) The smaller brush head also allows me to reach places the larger Spinbrush cannot reach, because it's too big. The Vitality is easier to maneuver in your hand as well, thanks to the smaller handle base.  Another thing I didn't like about the Spinbrush is how it would click off automatically after 2 minutes (I don't think all models of the Spinbrush do this, though.) The Vitality purposely sputters after 2 minutes for it's timing function, but then continues it's normal operation after a second or two. I still find this annoying, but at least I don't have to remove it from my mouth, dripping with toothpaste, just to turn it back on. And if I finish early, the Spinbrush required me to punch the button twice to stop it (again, something not easy to do with a vibrating toothbrush in your mouth), whereas the Vitality only requires a single button push. These two things alone make the Vitality much more convenient.  I also think the Vitality is more powerful then the Spinbrush. The reason you had to push the button on the Spinbrush twice was so you could use it at a lower speed if necessary, but I never found that necessary at all. I prefer the more powerful Vitality, because it feels like it's cleaning better by not slowing down if I push too hard.  About the only thing I liked better about the Spinbrush was that it had an indicator light on the base to tell you it was receiving power (I think it gauged the charge, too, but that was never a problem for me.) I'm not sure if that's even important, but it is something I tend to prefer with rechargeable items. Other than that, I love the Vitality and I much prefer it over the Spinbrush. Now I can brush my teeth without gagging and I am thankful for that

review: Nice salon-quality cuticle pusher with nail cleaner tool, with a minor caveat.. I have been looking for a stainless steel cuticle pusher to use for home manicures - this one is nearly identical to the one used by my manicurist, it has a nice weight to it, is comfortable to use, and is salon-quality.  I use it with the CND CuticleAway Cuticle Remover gel, and it works just as expected.  The nail cleaner end is a nice touch - I prefer this style to the ones that have flat or split trimmer blade ends.  One caveat - the edge on the pusher end is sharp - you need to be careful of the pressure and angle used which pushing your cuticles back, as holding the tool at the wrong angle and/or using too much pressure may result in damage to the top layer of your nail (e.g. the tool may shave a slight bit off). I used my Dremel with a fine sanding bit to dull the edge on the pusher end; this resolved the issue for me. If you don't have a Dremel, I suggest taking an emery board to smooth the sharp end before use in order to avoid damaging your nail.  I paid FULL price for this cuticle pusher, and did not receive any incentives or discounts in exchange for this review

review: A fairly basic 'stache wax with good hold and tackiness. I'm the proud owner of a rather glorious handlebar moustache (though I say so myself). So when a 'stache wax or grooming product comes available on Vine I'll usually request it if it's anything in the neighborhood of what I usually like.  I like firm or strong hold waxes with significant tackiness. I won't even consider a wax unless it either states a strong hold or a tacky hold or both. As a reference my other favorite common varieties of moustache wax include (in order of preference descending): Firehouse Moustache Wax - Tacky (Wacky Tacky) The Vintage Grooming Company - Death Grip Can You Handlebar - Primary  All of these are either exceptionally tacky or very strong in hold or both. I have tried many other waxes by various brands over the last several years but the ones above are my favorites and the ones that I feel are most worth mentioning in comparison to this product.  I would rate this wax as slightly less tacky than the Firehouse Moustache wax Tacky and slightly less stiffness than the Can You Handlebar Primary wax. Death Grip has it's own unique and weird properties (and I don't love the way it smells) so it is hard to direct compare :-)  As far as my general ranking I'd put this solidly in the top 5 waxes I've ever tried though, probably just under the three above and maaaybe 5th place after maybe Fisticuffs Strong Hold (which also has some pine resin for stickiness).  Unscented is good! Nothing worse than a cloying scent right up under your nose holes all day long!  Anyway, it has a strong hold for shaping if you like a strong curl as I do, combined with a tacky hold if you get a lot of stray and fly away hairs as I do. While my "go to" product is still Firehouse Tacky, and this has not replaced that, this is a worthy offering. The tree embossment on the wax is cute and I kinda dig that they give you the recipe.  The price point at the time of this writing is very fair. If you're in need of a good strong hold tacky wax I'd say give this product a shot!

review: Lovely Staub quality, WATCH description idiosyncrasies. Go to Staub's website for product details and why this French-made Enameled Cast Iron Dutch Oven is the best of the best and is over superior quality.  However, I will explain at the end how to correctly judge this description and know what you will get (you still won't be disappointed).  Yes all good features of a quality dutch oven. It has a tight sealing lid, proprietary basting spikes, nickel steel handle. The best part is the matte black enameled interior, this not only reduces the staining effects that are normal for enameled cast iron (I never understood why people complained about darkening Le Creuset, this is normal), but we have improving non-stick. Enameled CI REDUCES not eliminates sticking, and is acid safe to prevent iron leeching with low & slow acidic cooking.  You will find that the matte black interior improves with very light oiling with of a neutral tasting oil with relative high smoke oil (I tend use non-virgin Sunflower or Canola). This is somewhat like cast iron, but to a lesser extent. I just think of it with improvement with use  My two Staub's 7 and 4.5 QT get a majority of my Dutch Oven use, they are my go-to work horse. However, I would offer to consider purchasing a mid-size cast iron dutch oven as well.  I do have an unlined 4.5 QT  Lodge Signature cast iron dutch oven, but I tend to NOT use it for soups and most braising, especially highly flavored ethnic dishes.. When I do it's only for certain uses it's better suited over enameled. I like when I break it out for a comfort food of Chili (any good Texan will tell you NO beans), very high heat (>450-500+), rustic breads that benefit from CI, and deep fat frying. review: Yes, these really work...but keep a few things in mind. After very minimal and barely noticeable success with whitening toothpastes and gels, I finally decided to give Crest Premium Whitestrips a try.  Previously, I had found the cost to be prohibitive, but the fact that $5 or $7 coupons are offered in our Sunday paper with some regularity made the price a bit easier to swallow.  Just like the commercials say, I definitely did begin to see some improvement after about three days.  I would describe the effect as more of a lightening than a whitening per se:  the darker yellow spots on my teeth began to fade and to become less apparent.  Now, after using the product as prescribed for a week, the color of my teeth is clearly improved; I wouldn't say that my teeth are bright white, but they are definitely more of an ivory or a paler yellow color.  According to the package insert, you can immediately begin a second course of treatment for even better whitening effects, but I haven't yet decided if I want to lay out another $30 in order to do this.  Also, I should mention that the effect is not so dramatic thta anyone has noticed (UNLIKE in the commercials!).  Now for the caveats.  First of all, I found these strips to be a bit difficult to use.  It can be hard to remove the strips from the protective backing without them becoming mangled, and it is very easy to get the gel on your fingertips (which causes a temporary whitening effect).  Also, the strips are not ideally shaped for your mouth, and I found that they covered my front eight teeth only.  Finally, while the top strip adhered fairly well, I found that the bottom strip was more tricky and tended to slide around, especially if I moved my mouth at all.  The only solution I found to this was to wear the strips while commuting to work, which luckily gave me a 30-minute period when I did not need to talk.  Otherwise, it can be difficult to find a good time to wear the strips, as the insert information advises against wearing them immediately after you brush your teeth, while sleeping, and while you are eating/drinking.  Unlike other reviewers, I did not have a problem with the taste of the strips:  I could not detect anything while wearing them, and after taking them off, I thought that the gooey paste left behind was virtually tasteless.  I did experience some sensitivity in a lower tooth which I had capped over 20 years ago.  Although this sensation went away in time, it was uncomforable enough to make me cut the lower strip to fit around this particular tooth.  In summary, I did see clear--although not miraculous--results from this product and I would be willing to try the strips again, especially if the price were to come down a bit.  Ultimately, I would rate Crest Whitestrips three and a half stars, as there is definitely room for improvement

review: Snozzle with Xtava Black Orchid and Conair Infinity Pro. Similar to some of the other reviewers experiences, I find that the SnozzlePro works pretty well for me, but I do have to be very careful and make frequent adjustments -- it sort of exploits design problems with the tools you are using. I used it with a Conair Infinity ProPro and an Xtava Black Orchid.  Pros: -It definitely fits my Conair Infinity Pro and probably won't have any trouble fitting other hair dryers. -It's thick enough to be sturdy, but thin enough that I can stretch it onto the hair dryer. - I don't experience any leaking or weird smells. -I can use it (carefully) with the Xtava.  Cons: -It is made of rubber, so when it heats up the rubber becomes more pliable and loose around the diffuser. I would recommend using this with cold air if possible. Unfortunately, my Conair Infinity Pro has a setting for "Cool" that isn't cold enough. So, I find that this works best if I keep my finger on the blue "Cold Shot" button the whole time. -The Xtava has a very short connection point, so even though the SnozzlePro works pretty well, there's not a ton of space for it to hold on. That's a problem with the Xtava though, not the SnozzlePro. In particular, it seems to detach most at the top of the connection point and it will fall off while I'm using it. I just sort of use it gently and keep an eye on that top part to make sure it isn't slipping out.  Overall, I think the SnozzlePro is a great product that would probably work best with a diffuser with a longer connection point than the Xtava and potentially a hair dryer that has a truly cold setting

review: Took Care of My Brassy Hair the First Time I Used It!. A few weeks ago, I tried a different brand of purple conditioner. review: Pretty good coverage for a powder. First time in 20 years I've transitioned from a liquid concealer to a powder, the coverage is obviously not the same but this is by far the best performing powder I've ever had. I'm lucky in that my face at it's not-the-most-tan tiny works well with the light color but I can see how the limited color choices can be a deal breaker for some. It's smooth and not cakey, it blends well, feels weightless, and stands up to sweating and long work days with great shine prevention and it doesn't come off easily (a little when you blow your nose etc). I do not like the porcelain doll look and this works well for me for evening out tones.  I am 35 and have very sensitive skin, several minor facial scars, and occasional adult acne and this doesn't have any negative effects on my skin at all. It washes off easily with gentle face wash. It allows for a few spot touches of stick concealer, blends well, and holds well. Mine arrived with no breaks/cracks and the sponge works well. I really like the protective inner plastic case between the powder and the lid and sponge. Will buy again! I previously used Revlon, Covergirl, Neutrogena, and JUNGSAEMMOOL Essential Star-cealer Foundation which I was happy with the first time and then the following two were slimy and just not working well. For reference my current face tone is a revlon 300-310, a covergirl 705-710, and Starcealer Light. After peak summer I'm a more 310-320, 710-715, and Starcealer Medium (almost, its still a little dark for me)

review: Why didn't they add another magnet, so you can trim them?. This was my first magnetic eyeliner and eyelash kit. The eyeliner works great and the lashes adhere very well. The eyelashes themselves are beautiful and I love the lengths. The liner is easy to put on and so are the lashes. And, they stay on very well, with one exception.  The eyelashes are too wide for my eyes, and I need to cut the last magnet off for them to fit properly. But, when I do that the outer end flips up and makes the lashes look terrible. If I don't cut them, they stick into the inner corner of my eyes, causing major irritation and immediately flip up, also making them look terrible.  I feel like they need one more magnet on the outer end, close to the last magnet. Because, most people need to trim any and all eyelashes, in order to make them fit their eyes better. In every video I've ever watched with glue on lashes, the person always has to trim the eyelashes just a little bit shorter in width. Why didn't the manufacturers of these eyelashes think that it would not be the same for these lashes?  I love the concept, and really wish that these worked for me, because I have very dry eyes and cannot wear eye makeup and mascara. They just need another magnet!

review: Wash them well before using 💀. A spray bottle is a spray bottle, right? 🤔 Lol, nope!  So, here we are... shopping on Amazon, presented with a thousand options for something as simple as a bottle that sprays. 😰  My selection criteria was this: (a) The plastic must be able to handle liquid sanitizer made with a base of 60% alcohol (the 91% ISP variety), *without suffering undesirable changes* and (b) Have a good spray nozzle capable of producing a fine, even mist *without getting clogged*.  This set of bottles from MOSTOF checks both of those boxes. ✔ I tested them specifically against 2 different types of liquid (not gel) sanitizer.  Initially, I chose this particular set for the larger sized funnels that are also included, and the fact that it comes with (10) travel sized bottles.  None of my bottles leak and they spray a fine, even mist without leaving droplets.  After seeing the spray function in action, I decided to use a couple of these for facial mists and essences. I don't know (yet) whether they'll spray every last drop, but the sprayer feed wraps all the way around the bottom of the bottle, which does look promising. 🤞 So far, every liquid I've put in them has been fine; the plastic didn't change and the sprays perform the same.  Ultimately, I had to dock a star from my rating because the bottles came filthy inside, 😬 every one of them is heavily scratched up, and one of the bottles I received doesn't sit evenly. ➡️(see photos 3&4: defect (warped) bottle is on the right)⬅️  PRO'S: + Contains everything you need to package liquids immediately + Includes larger sized funnels = quick flow in filling + Spray nozzles produce fine, even mist without leaving droplets + Sprayer feed goes all the way around the bottom of the bottle + No leaking from the bottle necks or spray nozzles + Spray nozzles have not clogged + Caps fit tightly + No adverse reactions to the plastic (re: high alcohol content) + Airline approved carry-on size + Excellent price for ten bottles (and two funnels!) + Convenient PRIME shipping + Bonus sheet of labels (they're small, but they work)  CONS: - Bottles came really scratched up and very dirty - One of the ten bottles I received doesn't sit evenly  SUMMARY: Ultimately, I think there's some quality control issues that the manufacturer could improve upon. As long as you're not an Etsy seller, or someone that's gonna be gifting these, you may not mind the scratches or the possibility of uneven bottom(s). Provided you wash them out really good, they still do the job! 👍🏼 Should anything happen to change with these as time goes on, I will update this review. Thanks for reading! Stay safe. 😷

review: Never Knew My Feet Could Be So Soft!. My feet are so horribly dry and cracked,  they look like funky fish scales.  I was anxious to see if Monikahair's foot peel mask could help.  The process is incredibly easy and requires next to no work.  Prior to starting, I cleaned my feet. ( The lotion for the treatment is already in the socks).  I then placed a plastic 'sock' over each foot and used the tape on each sock to seal them closed.  The instructions say to keep the socks on for 60-90 minutes but I got wrapped up in an episode of 90 Day Fiance and kept them on for 2 hours. lol. The lotion did not cause any issues for me...I have extremely sensitive skin and had no reaction of any kind to the lotion. It did not cause burning/itching, etc.  When the time was up, I removed the socks and cleaned my feet.  Here's what happened:  Day 1 (the day after I did the treatment)-nothing  Day 2-VERY light peeling-more like little 'threads' of skin  Day 3-Actual peeling -I was pulling some decent pieces of skin off of both feet  Day 4-WOW...BIG pieces of peeling skin! (unfortunately, I had already started to peel off the skin when I remembered to take a picture for this review...the picture does not show just how much peeling had actually taken place)  Day 5-Very little peeling-mainly on toes  Day 6-Next to no peeling  Day 7 & 8-No peeling at all  Results:  The bottom of my feet are soft and pink with the exception of my heels. Those are my trouble areas. Calluses are very thick and cracked on my heels.  (a million times worse during winter months!) I DID have some progress on my heels but nowhere near the rest of my feet.  I used the scraper (? not sure if that's what it's called) and made a bit of progress.  I wish now that i had wiped some of the lotion directly on my heels when I wore the socks.  When I do my next treatment, I will absolutely rub some lotion directly on my heels when I start.  I'm impressed and thrilled with the results.  Its flip flop season and my feet aren't always pretty to look at.  This foot peel really helped.  I absolutely recommend Monikahair foot peel if your feet are dry and cracked. They're going to look and feel SO much better after using this treatment! (I told my mom about my success and she already ordered one of herself !lol )  Photos:  #1-wearing the 'socks', #2- day 2, #3-day 4, #4-finished  Day 5

review: Very thin lotion with an unpleasant initial fragrance. I love trying different lotions, particularly those that have nice fragrance, but when I received this set, I almost threw it away!  I the bottle, the smell of the lotion is horrible - I found it to have a strong, artificial scent similar to alcoholic spirits.  I decided to give it a try so that I could write an accurate review.  The "lotion" is quite thin, much more watery than any other moisturizer I have used.  Just to spread on my elbows requires at least 10 pumps from the tiny bottle.  The good news is that once on the skin, the distasteful fragrance does not last; I didn't really detect much scent at all after that, but there may have been a faint hint of rose in the dry-down.  The moisturization was adequate, nothing more.  I do like the Nail & Cuticle Oil, which comes in a little roller bottle and actually DOES have a rose scent.  But this set is absolutely NOT worth the cost, especially given that the lotion is likely to be completely gone after just a few weeks of daily use.  Not recommended.  NOTE:  At least one other reviewer ("Jam Blaster") mentioned the same issue with the lotion smelling bad and gave this product just 1-star as a result.  UPDATE, 2/1/21: Since I don't like the scent of this product, I decided to try it on my feet.  Despite the lotion being very thin, I actually found it to work quite well on my feet!  I put it on in the a.m., then put on socks; by the end of the day, my feet definitely felt soften and smoother.  I think the product is too expensive to purchase for this reason alone, but it does work, and so I increased my rating to 3-star

review: A Very Nice Hydrating, Soothing, Barrier-Repairing Antioxidant Cream. (Ingredients list is at the bottom of this review.)  I have really enjoyed using the Celleanser Vegan Clean Cream, and my skin seems to like it too. I also tried the Celleanser Clean Toner Mist, and the Celleanser Clean Serum. They all worked nicely for my dry, sensitive skin, and they worked nicely together.  This cream has a thick and creamy texture. It is very smooth and soothing to apply to the skin. It soaks in well, but it doesn't disappear. It leaves a nice layer of extra hydration and moisture on the skin. Though, it is lightweight and breathable. Not heavy at all. It is not sticky, and it layers perfectly with other products. The scent is sort of lightly herbal or earthy, similar to many Korean skincare brands.  I will say that the finish isn't my go-to. It isn't really dewy or glowy. But I wouldn't call it extremely matte either. Maybe somewhere in-between, but more toward the matte side. I typically like to use dewy, glowy skincare, so I would probably use this product at night for that reason.  The packaging is a nice 60ml tube with a flip-top cap. A little goes a long way, and I imagine this tube will last me a while. At $19.99 for 60ml / 2.02 fl. oz., it's an excellent deal. Especially because the ingredient list is nice.  I haven't been using it long enough to speak on the long-term results, but I do like the cream so far, and I will definitely continue to use it. review: Cute MOM gift but not as fragrant or impressive as I expected. [[VIDEOID:f77804a8088c40dfbef6fdcfacf8b15a]] There are three individually wrapped bath bombs in this set along with one bar of hand soap and a package of dried rose petals. In total there are five items. The bath bombs spell MOM with the heart substituting for the letter O.  The outside packaging looks giftable but the inside is just an ordinary uninspiring throw-away box. The fragrance of the bombs and soap is hardly noticeable. It has a whisper of rose aroma and I detect no lavender at all. I did try the letter M bomb in a hand bath and it dissolved in 5 minutes in lukewarm water and a nice foam of suds lasted about 10 minutes. The results initially felt moisturizing because my hands felt a little oily after the hand bath; however, eventually I needed to moisturize my hands with lotion.  With regard to the dried petals, one has to like something like that in their bath because it requires straining the water so that they don't go down the drain. For me, I would never use petals in a bath, so keep the recipient in mind when ordering this.  The bar of soap is the only item that would be used by most people.  One thing I love is that the color of the dissolved bomb did not adhere to my skin, my hand bath, or my towel. That is not always the case with bath bombs today.  The current price of $9.74 ($12.99 minus 25%) comes to $1.95 per item which is reasonable

review: Wide variety of designs (none repeated!) will keep the kids happy as long as they last…. …which is hardly more than a sleep or two at most, but that's okay because there are approximately a gazillion of these cute, kid-friendly tattoos, or so it seems: four themed packets (sea life, circus, zoo/wildlife, and insects) each contain ten tattoo sheets, and each sheet contains a dozen or so tattoos for 430 total.  Sheets are not perforated so individual tattoos must be cut out—carefully, by an adult or older child.  No instructions are included but they work like any temporary tattoos: after cutting each one out, peel off the plastic and apply face down (i.e., with blank paper backing on top), saturate with water, and, while holding it still, apply some pressure to facilitate the transfer—a thumbnail will work, as will any smooth, rounded hard tool such as a worry stone or a gua sha body scraper.  These are not super-durable; I was able to remove one pretty easily an hour after application by rubbing my bare fingertip back and forth over it a bit of force. Careful children may make them last a couple of days by guarding them from unnecessary contact; more rambunctious ones will likely discover they disappear much sooner.  Bottom line: Great at a party or to give out individual sheets as party favors; we'll be using them at "cousins' camp" for a dozen boys and girls ages around 4 to 10, so the variety of styles and subjects is a major plus for wide-ranging appeal

review: Would love to be able to give them 5 stars. I was really so excited when I got this package. I have ordered magnetic lashes on Amazon prior but this was really the nicest set I've received, by far. You get the lashes, cleanser, cotton cloths, the applicator and liner. The lashes were some of the nicest looking I've seen as well. I especially loved how natural they looked, because the magnets are not as big and bulky.  The liner is super smooth and goes on well.  For those reasons I would easily give the lashes a five star. For ease of use, I had to go down to a four, because while they are easy to put on, it isn't easy to get them to STAY on.  This is where I'm perplexed, and why I didn't give them a high mark for value. While I love my lashes to look great, it's equally as important, if not more so that they stay on, or what good are they? I put multiple layers of the liner and firmly applied the lashes. I thought it may be the smaller magnets.  So, I tried a different magnetic liner and I will say, the lashes stayed about twice as long with the other liner, but still not as long as competitors, that stay for about 12 hours.  I am actually really disappointed because visually, and set contents-wise these are my favorite.  I'm hoping maybe I just got a mad tube of liner, but it isn't worth it for me to purchase another set that may be useless to me. review: Best and Best-Buy Electric available today. In spite of the fine reviews, when I ordered it I was skeptical. I'm a believer now. I also am always skittish when I hear of a product that tells you "time to buy more".. :)  Also the purchase of replacement heads CAN be reasonably priced IF you buy it from amazon rather than a vendor that needs added shipping AND you plan ahead to  fit it into another purchase so you get free shipping (or even possible discounts). They are currently priced about $15 for 3 and that seems reasonable. (or you may find them at a "store near you" at retail price which I would expect to be similar).  PRO: *The DUAL CLEAN provides excellent cleaning. *For those with small mouths or special needs there are other heads available for whitening, flossing, soft bristle, and single rotating *The battery SEEMS to be pretty long-lasting (based on others, I've not had it long enough to judge) *reasonably priced and available head replacements *the built-in 2 minute timer is also a nice feature *the charger is small and functional (too tall for most medicine cabinets..). The cord is plenty long. *Its easily rinsed  CON: *The rechargeble battery SHOULD be specially disposed of (think green) *The dual head is fairly large.. its fine for me, but for children or small mouths I expect it would be uncomfortable (use a different head style) *The "buy now" color-change bristle seems to vary only with time, not use or bristle flexibility.. It is pretty much just a marketing gimmick.. buy a new one when you think you need it instead.  I've examined a number of electric brushes (and have owned a number over the last 30 years) and I believe this to truly be the best on the market to date.  edit 7/'11: The price on this has gone up almost $12! This is a 66% increase in a year.. There has been no retooling cost .. they are just milking a cash cow now.. I got a bad haircut a week ago and wasn't able to leave my house, was super depressed, crying all the time when i saw a mirror. This wig is a great solution as the semester is starting in one week and I absolutely have to be on campus. It's less hot than other wigs I have, and I feel confident that this looks natural enough to pass as I start meeting new people at my new school. One thing though is that the wig I received is NOT lace front. Since I gave it full bangs, that doesn't really matter, and I don't care that much about that in general because I will make sure to have bangs with any wig, but I thought it would be lace front and it would have been my first so I was disappointed it wasn't. review: Softest hands ever, lightly scented w/ lemongrass oil, lemon oil, orange oil, rosemary. I love Leap bar soaps (LOVE!), and was curious about their liquid hand soap. It is a 12 ounce pump style bottle with visually pleasing label. The soap comes out thick and rich. It is super luxurious feeling- it lathers significantly all the while feeling like hand cream. It rinses well and leaves skin feeling soft. Probably the most soft. Perhaps a little coating of glycerin and aloe are left behind? Yet not a gross coating.  I am trying to figure out the magic of my soft, smooth, clean feeling hands on a super cold (18*F), dry day. Super moisturizing.  Oddly, I find it has barely any scent. I am used to their super scented bar soaps, and I was expecting a stronger scent to come through. I am not usually keen on perfume (causes headaches, nausea), but when a product uses essential oils for scenting (especially hand soap and house cleaners), I find it delightfully uplifting. This is labeled as lemongrass, but that isn't the only essential oil used. The profile is more complex with the addition of lemon oil, orange oil, and rosemary. I was really excited for this to have a robust citrus smell. I really couldn't tell you just by sniffing. It smells fresh and clean, but it isn't strong (and I was hoping/expecting strong). I see other reviewers mentioning a strong smell. I figured I got a weird bottle or I have covid. I actually went and grabbed my Leap bar soap to make sure I could still smell that. I can. Phew.  I'm still going 5 stars because it does have a mild fresh scent, and the soap itself is glorious. Very rich, super moisturizing lather. And it rinses away perfectly. I dont feel like I am working to get the soap off. If it did, I wouldn't like that. So there is some sorcery involved here, lol. I kinda want it as a body wash. My hands feel SO GOOD after using this. I just keep touching my hands.  One does not need a lot of soap, so feel free to just add a little to the hand. I would even go so far as to add a little water as it goes down. Or if you like this soap and have a foamer, then just a wee bit of this with a lot of water will do it.  Love their designs on the bottles.  Water, Organic Coconut Oil, Organic Olive Oil, Vegetable Glycerin, Organic Guar Gum, Lemongrass Oil, Orange Oil, Organic Jojoba Oil, Lemon Oil, Rosemary Extract, Organic Aloe Vera (Potassium Hydroxide is used to saponify the organic oils into soap, but none remains in the final product)

review: This products contains the toxic chemicals methylene chloride and methanol.. There has been much discussion about this product on Amazon and professional nail tech blogs.  One of the most serious issues is the absence of a safety data sheet (SDS) from the manufacturer.  By law, manufacturers selling chemical products in the United States must provide accurately documented SDS upon request.  The manufacturer of this product has not provided such a SDS.  We ordered a product through Amazon which arrived via China Post/USPS identified as 'Makeup Tools' for customs purposes.  As professional chemists, we analyzed this product (pH, FTIR, TGA, elemental analysis and GC-MS).  This alkaline product contains methylene chloride, methanol, n-butoxyethanol, a series of n-alkane hydrocarbons and two different petroleum boiling point distillate fractions.  Methylene chloride and methanol are known toxic chemicals which can be absorbed through the skin and inhaled into your respiratory tract.  Please use Google to search for and open the SDS docs for these two chemicals and read the hazards.  This product is similar to a methylene chloride containing industrial paint strippers which are being removed from the marketplace due to their toxic ingredient(s).  This product is not suitable for sale to the general public or to the professional nail community as a nail polish remover.  AMAZON is derelict in its duty to police the products it sells; in this case the product is highlighted as "Amazon's Choice".  Please be aware that there are other brands of 'Magic Remover' being offered for sale with a similar name, paper label and bottle shape.  Buyer Beware!

review: Gold Themed Beauty Box. This "facial kit" has all the items you'd expect to get in a spa gift basket, only it's shipped in a cardboard box reminiscent of subscription boxes. The main difference is that it's a one-time deal, no subscription needed, and all the items are grouped together by theme and color. I ordered the "gold" theme and was a little disappointed that not all the items are gold colored (the eye mask is blue) and there's a mix of drugstore items with some more luxurious feeling ones.  I'll start with the good. The box is very cute, with the words "It's a great day to love your face" greeting you when you open the box. Inside you get a five count box of sheet Masks that contain retinol, a generous and thick box of facial wipes, a Gold under-eye pad to reduce lines and puffiness, and a gold Lip Mask (I've never used a "lip mask" before so this seems a little bizarre, if fun). The blue eye mask is filled with gel beads so you can use it hot or cold, and the cheapest and least impressive items are the "facial buff" (a pear-shaped sponge that looks like something you'd clean your pots with) and a  "facial cleansing brush" that looks a little cheap but is nevertheless useful.  The main thing that was missing was some packing peanuts or confetti, as the items were tossed into the box hither and thither with NO padding, whereas other gift baskets and boxes typically include some stuffing so that the items are more artfully displayed. This one wasn't, so if I were giving this to someone as a gift, I'd certainly add it so the items wouldn't arrive in a jumble. But otherwise, I liked it

review: Patience required. I’ve been trying out a couple of different lash serums over the past month. With my husband also using it (on his brows), while I use it on my lashes, we’ve been able to try different brands to see if there are any differences in results. This serum, by Kimuse, is very similar to the others in consistency (a thin liquid) and in how it’s applied (with a very thin brush). I have had no negative reactions to the serum, and no irritation to my eyes even when I’ve slipped and gotten some in my eye. This serum boasts results in as little as 3-4 weeks, while most others are more conservative at 6 weeks. In the few weeks we’ve been using the serums, neither of us have noticed any dramatic changes as far as lash or brow growth, but I do think I’m losing fewer lashes which is a definite plus. Honestly, I’m not sure if any serum is going to provide dramatic results, but we’ll continue for at least a few more weeks and see what happens while hoping for the best.Hopefully, I’ll be back with exciting news!  Update: After using this, as well as other, lash growth serums for several months, I have noticed a definite improvement in the length of my lashes. I have not noticed as significant an improvement in the thickness, or volume, of my lashes, however. I believe that these types of serums do help promote growth, and I haven't been able to detect much difference between brands except that a couple of them irritated my eyes. Therefore, my conclusion is that this is helpful and the real determination of what works best will be what's most comfortable for you to use, so read the ingredients and watch for any possible allergy triggers or irritants

review: Cool once you get the hang of it....but the price.... I'm someone with extremely thick and stick straight hair.  My hair loses curl within an hour of me fixing it.  I've tried other rotating curling irons and haven't had much success with them, so I didn't have very high expectations for this beach waver.  I have been pleasantly surprised.  Once I got the hang of it, I found it to be pretty easy to use.  It features buttons that allow you to chooses which direction you would like to curl each section of hair, and a Home button that after each use, and after the previous section of hair is no longer attached, allows the barrel to return to a neutral starting point.  I ran into an issue the first few times I used it, which was accidentally hitting the home button while my hair was still around the barrel.  This caused the hair to get very tight and the barrel to press up against the scalp.  This is very easy to do and I definitely think a design change should take place to correct this issue.  The barrel is long enough for my medium-long hair and I can see it needing to be used more than once up and down the length of long hair.  The curling iron gets up to 410 degrees max, which works pretty well on my thick hair.  I've tried fixing my hair in different ways after using it, to see which method holds the curls longer.  I still have an issue with my hair losing the curls a bit to quickly but it's remedied by using styling products before and after curling it.  To be honest, I think this beach waver is very overpriced.  Maybe the results would be better for someone with thinner hair but I don't think I'd pay more than $50 for this curling iron.  Nice results, but the design flaws make this a product I won't reach for that often

review: Works great if a "good" shave is acceptable.. I have never wanted an electric razor, but at 55, I decided that one might work with my current lifestyle. I'm more or less retired, so I don't have to shave every day, and when I do shave, I'm no longer obsessive that the shave be perfect in all areas. I'm finally mellowing, I guess. This set of razor and other tools gives a pretty amazing shave for the price of the bundle, and after learning not to press it into my skin, I've gotten a lot of acceptable shaves in the couple of months I've owned this Surker shaver.  I've tried it different ways, but my favorite is to use Williams' Lectric Shave lotion, then gently shave.  This electric razor doesn't give a perfect shave under my jaw line, where I have always had to use a regular razor in several different directions repeatedly to get the shave good and close under there.  But, but using a circular motion clockwise under my jaw and on my neck, then counter-clockwise, the shave is close enough that I'm the only one who knows there's still a bit of stubble there. In short, it isn't a perfect shave, but it's a good enough, acceptable shave, and faster and easier shaves than my decades of double and triple blade razors with soap, water, and shaving cream. For the price, this is a great set that does a fine job, and I like knowing I can buy replacement rotary shaving heads for it for less than $15 in the future

review: Not a loofah, but still a great wash cloth.. This is a great wash cloth, but it's not a loofah, so the name might be a little misleading to some. A loofah is a natural sponge that's light tan in color and much rougher than this,  which is a super soft terrycloth wash cloth on one side and 'bath poof' material on the other. I still like it very much, but didn't buy it expecting a loofah. It's nice and big so I can wash my back pretty easily with it. I'm not quite sure how anyone could keep it flat on their back like the picture shows though. Believe me, I've tried lol. The loops that you hold on to aren't straight across from each other, they're on diagonally opposite corners so the cloth tend to roll up significantly when you use it on your back. I think another reviewer referred to it as 'burrito-ing'  which I think describes it perfectly. Regardless of that, it still washes really well, makes a ton of lather and stays soapy fora good long time. It's awesome for washing my feet. I don't have to balance on one foot like a flamingo to clean the bottom of each one. I just lift my foot a little, put this underneath it and use the loops to pull it back & forth. I'm really happy that the package came with 2, so when this one inevitably wears out I'll have another one waiting to take its place.  I did receive a discount on this product in exchange for an honest review, but all opinions are 100 percent my own. review: GReat Bronzer For Medium To Lighter Skin Tones, But Great Eye Shadow Too- Read On. As a makeup artist, I am always trying to find ways to get the most mileage out of the products that I use.  This bronzer had some surprises to it.  Read on..  PHOTO- My photo has swatches of both color 1 and 2 which are labeled.  I tried to get accurate photos colorwise and it is hard to do as the camera does not capture the nuances.  When applied with a brush, the effect is MUCH lighter.  WHAT IS THIS LIKE? COMPACT The compact is a high layered cardboard with a strong hinge to it.  There is no mirror and the pan inside has the product with designs pressed into it.  It does not come with a brush.  WHAT IS THE COLOR LIKE? This color is more of a bronze gold color.  It is still on the cooler side, but light warmer skin tones could use this too.  TYPE OF SKIN TESTED ON? This was tested on both MAC translation of skin tones NW 25 (which is what you see in the photos) and NC37 which is a more tan but cooler skin tone.  HOW TO APPLY? This applies well but you have to be sure you find the right brush.  A stippling brush was the best way to get a natural look from this bronzer and highlighter.  It allows for subtle application so that it does not look like you have on too much.  If you use too dense of a brush, it is easy to get a stripe of glow on your face that others will see and it can really look odd.  You also need to get a fresh brush and blend it very well into your skin.  Apply this in the backwards 3 figure on each side of your face.  Imagine two 3s in a mirror image on your face with the tips and centers touching.  ANY OTHER USES? I found that this also makes a fabulous eye shadow.  I found it to be a perfect match with the other color in this series of number 2 which is a darker more rose brown color.  This is a great companion to that.  If this is all you have, It also makes a great eye shadow alone or with another lighter satin finish shadow or even a matte.  I would not go super frosty.  HOW TO APPLY TO EYES In terms of eyes, you can use this as a contour, all over color, or in combination with the other darker color of this Sungasm series or another set of shadows.  The application is best for a lighter look to use a teardrop shaped brush.  Then for a heavier look with more color, a flat eye shadow brush packing this gently into place over a good eye primer is the way to go.  For a quick application, you can also use a finger to apply and blend it with a brush or your finger  ANY IRRITATION PROBLEMS? I am VERY sensitive and did not have any problems with this product on the face or eyes.  THE BOTTOM LINE As long as you are willing to take some time to find the right brush for the application of this, this bronzer is a pretty color especially for cooler toned skin.  It is a good highlighter for darker skin tones as a highlighter, though.  This is beautiful on the face, eyes, and in tandem with the other color of this bronzer too.  MY RATING FIVE STARS.  This is a nice bronzer and I am surprised at how well it works on cooler skin tones, something that is not all that easy to find, especially in TWO colors of a collections

review: These are exactly what I need them to be. These are great!  No seriously, I'm thrilled to have these.  If you're like me and you make your own lotions and creams and scrubs and such, then you absolutely NEED these, at a good price, in pretty much exactly this size and here's why.  If you make lotion and you've done the tiniest bit of research, then you know the preservatives debate/dilemma/controversy and that's this--if you're going to have a big bottle or jar of lotion out on the counter, then it NEEDS a preservative.  But all the preservatives have twelve-syllable unpronounceable names, and people who like to keep their stuff a little bit more on the natural side don't like to use them.  And if you're like me and you don't mind the long names of whatever chemical you have do use to preserve it, you're never 100% positive you got the right amount.  Too much, and the lotion is unusable and irritating.  Too little and you can get bacteria, mold and yeast growing in your lotion, and that's lousy.  So if you don't want to use a preservative, everybody advises you to keep your lotion in the fridge.  Which is great, but what, I want to get out of the shower, trek out to the kitchen, use my lotion, and then put it back while I'm in a towel?  Enter these cool little things, which hold a couple of days worth of cream, which is exactly how long I feel okay having an unpreserved lotion out of the fridge.  So I make my lotion, pour 24 ounces of it into these little things, and pull one out every couple of days.  Really good deal.  Hope they're dishwasher safe.  I received these at a discount in exchange for an honest review, and I chose to review them because I expected them to be good, and they are

review: Cheap and effective permanent hair removal - with some annoyances. Overall - This device works fine and it's cheap.  Like many other ladies I'm a big fan of any kind of permanent hair removal and have had professional laser and electrolysis treatment (both Blend and pure Thermolysis) many times, when comparing to that I can confirm this unit works both in theory and in practice.  It hurts like crazy because it is Galvanic Electrolysis (the oldest and most classic type), which also makes a disturbing white foam ooze out of the follicle - that foam is actually Lye created by the electric current flowing through the natural liquid in your follicle and it's melting the hair and follicle lining on the way out, killing the hair permanently.  It makes loud obnoxious 7-second long beeps repeatedly as you use it which may drive a spouse or roommate crazy.  Each hair takes 2-3x as long to treat with this method compared to the way professionals do it, but it totally works.  Just don't expect to remove 6-10 hairs a minute like a professional, expect 2-3 instead.  It requires disturbingly wet and salty fingers holding the stylus which you have to frequently re-wet.  It's not suitable for anyone sensitive to electricity (which is to say, people with pace makers and some other conditions can not use this device).  But if you can deal with those quirks it is a very effective unit, and exactly what I expected as I was already familiar with the technology.  The gritty details - This device is a Galvanic Electrolysis unit, designed for use on self.  Galvanic Electrolysis works on the principle of using electric current to convert the liquid at the base of your hair follicles into Lye which is quite caustic and melts flesh in the area - in particular the goal is to kill the stem cells lining the follicle, so that the hair can never grow back.  These days you will rarely meet professional electrologists using Galvanic Electrolysis because it is both more painful and slower compared the now-ubiquitous Blend technology (Galvanic current and heat being delivered with the same stylus tip) or even plain Thermolysis (just heat).  The fact is that Electrolysis hurts like crazy and is a bit slow, but it kills the hair quite reliably, and some professionals still swear by it as being the superior technology - I don't have an opinion on that personally.  The technique for inserting the very thin tip next to your hair until it touches water is very well explained in the manual, and doesn't require as much dexterity as I thought - yes you have to be able to place the tip with millimeter precision and in the right direction so that it slides easily into the hair follicle, when you do this right (and have your fingers wet and salty enough while holding the stylus), you hear an annoying 7-second long beep.  You then hold it in there for another 7 second beep (and you can hold it longer than the recommended 15 seconds but you may raise welts and cause other temporary issues with the skin in the area).  The manual does a poor job of explaining the mere fact that this thing makes a beep when used successfully, and that you can easily test the unit by touching the tip to the touch plate on the base unit, which makes the expected beep - that was how I learned that yes my unit is fine and that I just had not put enough salt in the water I was wetting my fingers with (and they have to be quite wet but not quite dripping).  Some of my hairs released after 2 beeps with a gentle tug of my tweezers, as explained in the manual (although they just describe it as 15 seconds and not "wait for 2 beeps" which would have made more sense to me), but many took 3-4 beeps even at the higher settings (which can be excruciatingly painful).  Some ares are more sensitive than others, and if you find one is hurting a lot more than the others you should try turning down the settings and attack the other hairs in the area, failing to turn it down will result in welts around each treated hair but they fade after 30 minutes for me.  After the first beep I usually see a foaming white liquid begin to come out of the follicle, and the pain intensifies, each beep hurts more.  Ultimately this is all as expected.  To use this effectively on yourself you absolutely have to get a pair of jeweler's goggles or similar portable magnifier and light-source that will be practical to move around frequently.  Rather than getting a magnifying mirror to treat your face hairs I think it's more practical to have a friend treat those areas.  Also buy a pair of nice tweezers because the ones included are bordering on useless
