review: Better than many other epilators for smooth skin. I've tried a couple of different types of epilators over the past 15-20 years.  While I was usually happy enough with the results, I rarely used them since it always seemed like you had to wait until the hair got long enough for the unit to grip the hair in order to yank it out.  And rarely did I really want the hair on my legs to reach that amount of stubble.  Not to mention the pain that is involved with epilators.  Yes, I am a weenie.  This model of the Braun Silk Epil removes much shorter hair.  It claims to remove hair that is as short as a grain of sand (0.5mm).  I personally find it requires it to be a bit longer than that to grip; but it does do a much better job of reaching short hair than others I've tried.  It has a pivoting head which lets it work around all your body contours.  A light on the unit allows even the palest, finest hairs to be visible.  In addition to hair removal, this epilator refines your skin.  A sonic massage system and high-density brush scrub away old skin cells.  This exfoliation helps to stimulate the regeneration of surface skin cells in order to create a smoother skin tone.  I do notice a bit of a smoother, more even skin tone on my legs now.  This sonic massage is my favorite part of the device...in part because I really don't like the tweezing part.  This model can be used wet or dry and uses rechargeable batteries rather than a power cord.  Unfortunately, I find that it still hurts...although not nearly as much as it used to.  With regular use, the hairs on my legs have become fewer.  Plus, the already pale fine hair is becoming even thinner and weaker.  Braun claims that it will keep your body free of hair for up to 4 weeks.  I usually find it to be somewhere in the 2 to 3 week range for me.  Still, that's nice for when you're going on vacation or heading off to the beach for a week or two.  I allow the growth to get to the slight stubbly stage and then I'm perfectly smooth for a couple of weeks

review: Jagged plastic snags hair. These all look the same when they’re listed, so I just went with this one as it was the cheapest. Bad move? Maybe. There were seams of jagged plastic that my hair got tangled in. The “hands” didn’t line up perfectly, so there were weird gaps in the holes where the air came out, which my hair got stuck in and ended up losing a few strands. I then got my nail file and used the coarse grit side that I never use on my nails to “sand down” the rough edges from the seam, and around the holes. I had to keep sanding because I’d test it, feel the area that snags, and then file again. By the time I finished, the whole thing was sanded down and looking awful. Can’t return it now! I used it once it wasn’t snagging all my hair and breaking it off, and it did work. Heat was coming out of the “tips of the fingers” and my roots were dried, and the rest of my hair could air dry in all its undisturbed curl pattern glory. But it was still kind of snaggy and I was just so over sanding this thing as it took way longer than it should have, which honestly, it should have not had to be done at all! If I had to do it all over again, it’d just buy the bright green name brand one that was double (maybe more?) the cost of this, and not waste time screwing around with sanding this thing

review: It’s a decent idea, it worked, but not with the included suction cups. I drive my wife nuts when I trim my beard in the bathroom - I try to catch all the clippings, but without something like this, it does not work well. I thought I”d give this a try - it seems like a great idea, but...  1. It arrived with 1 plastic bib, 2 suction cups with hooks, and 1 shaving cream brush. 2. The plastic bib feels okay - it’s a thin plastic, but it should last for a decent amount of time. It is not as nice as most of the kinds I’ve experienced or we own for haircutting 3. Its stitching is okay - I think it’ll last decently 4. There are two loops on the ends you will attach to the suction cups. 5. The suction cups - are worthless. This is why it gets the 4 stars - I would have given it 3 stars if we didn’t have our own suction cups to use instead of theirs. One of the two that came with it stuck for 5 - 10 seconds before it stopped working altogether. The other suction cup doesn’t even look right - it looks like it never worked and was not made properly. 6. We have suction cups (bought on Amazon) we were able to use - I looped that part of the bib onto them, which worked, but not designed for this, they would fall off. I’ll end up taping them to it - at least that way I’ll be able to use it. 7. It fit me fine. It felt fine - just like a haircut cape. The white looks weird - I’m used to the far more common black - but at the same time I think it’ll show the beard hair really well. 8. I did notice that as I go in closer to the mirror to see what I’m doing it folds over in front of me and isn’t as trapped out - be aware of this because it’s easy to start missing the catch in the bib.  Overall it’s a decent thing to have and it’ll make my wife happy not getting the beard clippings all over the place. This could be a little nicer -  a little thicker plastic, much better suction cups - which would easily earn it a 5 star rating. But for what it is, I’m happy to have it. If it lasts, it’ll be great

First, the "on" and "turbo" buttons are too easy to push while handling, and I'm constantly startling myself with the turbo setting (it is a little loud).  Also, I find that the guide/vacuum design is poor.  This may work OK if you are trimming short guide settings, but if you get a clump of hair in the guide, which happens constantly with me, it will block the tiny opening for the hair cup.  The vacuum is not strong enough to pull the hair in, and it clogs the whole works.  If you do not notice this, the blockage will prevent the trimmer from trimming, and you may think that a lower guide setting is needed.  You can see how this sets you up for a scalp job when the low guide setting is finally low enough to make a cut.  I just find the whole set up "gimmicky" and I will take the old standard guides and no vacuum any day.  It does have a strong battery and if you are just lightly trimming a mustache or a beard, it may be the right choice for you.  I think people like me would not be disappointed (and would not have purchased the product) if it had been called the Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Beard and Mustache Vacuum Trimmer. review: DO NOT use for Sensitive Skin!. To start, I "manscape" periodically in the year, and I'm super pale. I have used 'Nair' on my skin before (legs), but I did not suffer chemical burns. Now, the instructions say to leave on no longer than 10 minutes and to test a small area first. I did this. Tested a small area of thick hair not far from the area to be 'scaped'. Wait at least 24 - 48 hours per section, or you will feel the flames of hell on your skin!) Doing the half and half interval of the area caused chemical burns. This was caused from overlapping cream and some areas being on my skin longer than 10 minutes while dealing with the burns of the overlap. The upside of the calming ball lotion, is that it works, but it's the ONLY lotion that eases the pain. I made the mistake of rinsing off the lotion and using skin repair lotion, which intensified EVERYTHING. Another lesson learned- apply the calming lotion after the rinse (and pat dry, don't wipe) and simply leave it. Seek medical attention of skin conditions appear or worsen.  Overall, the product did what it was meant to, but my hair was too thick; and my skin was far too sensitive for the chemical composition. review: Not for beginners. I was so excited to try the poly gel and thought it would be so easy but it wasn't that simple. You receive a set of 8 colors. The tubes are small so I'm not sure how many uses you'll get out of it. I think you'll get about 2 full uses per tube maybe 3. I had a hard time with this poly gel. I squeezed a small amount onto the nail former and smoothed it out evenly. I put a thin layer of base coat on my nail and cured it. Then I put the nail former filled with the poly gel onto my nail but it wouldn't stay in place. The former kept lifting from my nail. I tried putting more and putting less to see if it'll help the former stay in place but it didn't work. I cured it for 120 seconds twice and even then the center of my nail where the former lifted from didn't turn solid. I even have a couple bubble pockets. Also while curing, the poly gel flowed to the right side of the former and created a thick dried buildup underneath the nail. I think the shape of the former is what caused this and because the former needs to be lighter. I came to this conclusion because I have used another poly gel brand where the former was feather light and less curvy and was able to cure the gel completely and the former stayed in place until cured. I didn't have any buildup underneath my nail either and got it on the first try. Otherwise, the poly gel was very easy to shape after being cured. I used the clear and I love how natural it looks but it feels like I have an acrylic nail. I might use it in combination with the nail extention in the future. Hopefully that will stop the buildup from happening. It also comes with a free gift of glitter. Overall, the set it okay. May be better suited for more advanced users

review: A superb brace in all regards. I bought this brace after a fall in which I'd injured my knee, as well as my ankle, and needed to keep my knee completely immobile -- no lateral tuning or twisting at all, and restricted flexing and extension.  It was the third brace I ordered -- the first was not nearly strong enough, and the second sizing was off. I'm so glad I found this one: It's a superb brace -- fine, sturdy stays,plus hinges that let you adjust both flexion and extension. I initially thought that latter feature was something I wouldn't need, but it turns out to have made a huge difference during this first month of healing. (Needless to say, I could not have handled a sleeve-type brace -- the open front/wrap style was mandatory, and made my life so much easier.)  I've been wearing the brace 24/7 -- night as well as day --  for more than a month and it's been my saving grace.  Service has been superb, too: Before I ordered, I measured my thigh, knee and calf; I was on the cusp between sizes, and so ordered up. review: High-Quality Synthetic Hair Extension! Will Buy Again!. I was immediately enchanted with this hairpiece from the second I tried it on. I've tried wearing it a few days in a row now, and I'm not tired of it yet. First, I'll start by saying that I ordered it as an add-on item in "dark blue to peacock green." With Prime, it only took two days to get to my house; very fast and convenient shipping, and the hairpiece was encased in a clear plastic bag; I threw that away, as I keep my extensions in a silk hair case. This hairpiece is actually pretty high quality for synthetic, eccentric hair, so I would suggest something like that to keep it safe and untangled when you're not wearing it.  In my opinion, the product images do not really do this hairpiece justice. I can't say anything for other colors yet, but the dark blue to peacock green is pretty true to the product images, with sapphire blue roots and aqua-blue tips (although I will say the hairpiece I received is not half-and-half blue and green like the picture; mine is like an ombre gradient, approximately 2/3 blue and 1/3 aqua tips).  Many of the reviews here also have mixed comments on the thickness of the hairpiece; maybe the people who say it is "thin" are comparing it to their own natural hair? I will say that this piece is very thick for a single-weft hair extension. A weft is like a curtain of hair with a seam holding it all together at the top. I wear extensions almost every day after a butchered haircut took 12 inches of my hair. Authentic human hair extensions come in wefts of varying widths, usually one clip wide or four clips wide, and the hair is very thin because the wefts are meant to be layered on in sections, like natural hair. This blue hair extension is 5 clips wide--wide enough to fasten on your head from ear to ear. Because of my experiences with authentic human hair extensions, I was expecting this blue piece to be thin and underwhelming, but I was wrong and am very happy about that.  I also have an asymmetrical haircut that is close-cropped on one side, so this extension is actually too wide for me to wear across my nape (as the model does in the product image), but I am still able to use it. I curve it to clip from my left nape to above my right ear and it suits my needs and still looks real, despite its unusual color.  Since there is so much hair on a single weft, as other reviewers have stated, this hair extension is a bit heavy. That may take some getting used to, as improper clipping could cause some discomfort and irritation from pulling on the roots. However, once you get practice putting it in, you will learn the best way to clip it without any tugging or pulling of the hair.  It is synthetic material, and while I noticed that mine was shiny, it was not like "Barbie hair," as some reviewers said. I did not need to rub any baby powder in; I just wore it to work for a few hours a day and the shine eventually dulled to look a little less like synthetic material. I will try to add some photos to this page of what the extension looks like in my (straight black) hair. I also noticed that it became easily tangled after a few days of wear. This is not really a problem; I am afraid to brush it too often though, as it sheds (which is normal, but I want it to last).  Lastly, despite being synthetic material, I have tried straightening it on the high setting on my Conair flatiron with success. You can also use a razor or scissors to make any modifications to the style or length, if necessary.  Overall, I think you will be very satisfied with this product if you buy it. I liked it so much that I placed an order for dark pink/light pink and yellow/lime green. These were not add-on items, however, so I will be waiting until mid-August to September to receive these other hair extensions. Hopefully they will be as nice as the blue/peacock green, because I was not disappointed!

review: Cost Cutting Makes This Otherwise Good Shaver Fall Short. For years I've had a difficult time getting a close shave and a shave with minimal irritation.  I've tried several of the Mach 3 variants with little success.  Against or with the grain the Mach 3 would miss random places on my throat (especially around the adam's apple).  I quit the Mach 3 even though the shave was otherwise close because the irriation it left made me unable to make a second pass.  My Norelco Reflex Action series left me high and dry.  That's right, it didn't cut anywhere and left me burnt all over.  Most days it looked like I didn't even shave.  Angered over years of horrible shaving, I decided I would treat myself for my birthday.  I was seriously considering Brauns and Panasonic's high end razors but decided against it because there was no clearly outlined guarantee if it didn't get as close as I'd like.  Norelco on the other had advertises their's quite well and after reading a few reviews, I decided (...) I would take the plunge.  Here is my take after using a dry electric shaver for the past 2 years plus a weeks experience with the 7735x:  Pros: 1. Gets darn close for an electric.  Not quite Mach3 but more then satisfactory.  It does miss a bit around the adam's apple but nothing I can't live with. 2. Leaves me with almost no irritation.  In fact, I can shave 3 times a day with this thing if I feel like it!  Very impressed on the combination of closeness and lack of irritation. 3. Very easy clean up - just run under hot water. 4. Nivea lotion packs are easy to load and administer while shaving.  They also really contribute to the feel of the shave. 5. The shaver itself is well built and sturdy. 6. Quiet.  Cons: 1. Cost-Cutting abound!! 2. Cheap charging unit that does not automatically shut off after full charge is reached! 3. Ni-Cad batteries. 4. Cheap Strap for letting the shaver hang out and dry. 5. Cheap/useless carrying case. 6. The shaver's "cap" falls off too easily. 7. Norelco recommends you run the shaver to empty before recharging.  This can be a big problem if the battery runs dry and you need to shave - there's no way to plug the shaver into the wall and use it. 8. I can't for the life of me (and after reading the instructions 5 times) figure out how to get the shaving head off to put the trimmer attachment on.  Despite its near endless line of drawbacks, you do get a good shave with the 7735x.  I couldn't stop rubbing my neck and face after the first shave (and it seems the shave gets better the more I use it).  Oh yeah and the shocking part, I look forward to getting up at 6am just to shave! Yeah!

review: I like this but.... My only complaint with Zest isn't unique to that product:  it has to do with the downsizing of consumer products so companies don't have to raise their prices; they just give us less.  Zest comes in a 4 oz bar, common in most "bath sized" bars but smaller than I remember bars of soap when I was a younger man.  The smaller the bar, the easier it is to drop it when it's wet.  If you get beyond that, Zest has two strong positives:  the scent is pleasant without being overpowering.  It is appropriate for men but I don't think women would object to using it as well.  Also, it appears to be less caustic when you wash your face around your eyes.  I made the mistake of getting Coast Soap in my eyes once and almost had to see a doctor; this is much milder.  The bottom line:  I will continue to buy Zest and will keep whining about small bath bars.  This is a decent soap brand.  Update:  I originally wrote this about the 4 oz bars and the review somehow got applied to the larger 5 oz bars as well.  Please allow me to make this clear:  the 5 oz bars answers all the negatives I had about the smaller bars.  This is finally what I've been looking for and I couldn't be happier with the larger size.  I highly recommend it

SO, keep this in mind for where you want to use this and if you are comfortable with that length of blade. Otherwise it is all very similar.  I like that this 5 pack is contained within a box. Many are on a flat piece of cardboard with molded plastic around them. Makes it too easy to lose one, misplace one.. they just fall out of package when opened. This box will nicely store the remainder. I won't lose these among my other beauty goodies.  I have no idea what it says on the box. The sticker on the box says Made in China. The box says, Made in Japan. I can't read anything else.  Handle is short- I think adds to precision of use. The longer blade makes it harder to get the eyebrow area. For that, I would go with a smaller, angled razor. For larger areas of face (or other body areas), this large blade is nice. As with any blade, BE CAREFUL. And don't over use it- a dull blade can be as dangerous and damaging as a sharp blade.  The blade is indeed sharp. I usually use a regular razor (like for shaving legs) to shave my face. I have pale skin and dark hair, so I have always preferred to just shave off my hair. No, it doesn't grow back thicker or darker. But it sure makes the face nice and smooth- great for make up looking good, for skin care setting in nicely, for exfoliation- for overall health of skin. A leg razor is fine, less likely to cut.. but a straight razor provides an extra close shave (if careful). I love these for taking care of upper lip area, and for eyebrow area.. but is taking some getting used to since it is a longer blade than others I use

review: I love this toothbrush, but.... 1. I don't understand these reviews that complain about getting water into the battery compartment and corroding the batteries. I've never had this problem. It would seem that one would have to be really careless for this to happen. Don't submerge it or pour water over it, and you should be fine. 2. Don't worry about battery life. Get some Eneloop rechargeables, and swap them out anywhere from a couple weeks to a couple months and you'll be fine. 3. This does such a good job, my dentist assumes I'm flossing like I'm supposed to be. I'm not. I do use a waterpic, but only a couple times a week these days. My dentist gave me an A+ on my last visit (part of this is because of the fluoride rinse that's been helping strengthen my teeth, but that's another review).  So now to the reason I only gave it three stars.  I had one of these that we bought years ago. I don't remember how long, but it's been probably 5 years. I'm not exactly sure, but it's been awhile. It's always worked great and still does. We finally got tired of sharing, and when we saw they were only $20 on Amazon we got another one.  This second one has had to be replaced under warranty twice in about a year and a half. It just stopped working, both times. No corrosion in the battery compartment or anything. The unit looks pristine, it just stopped working.  The first one lasted about 8 months. The second one only about 6 months.  So while this is a great product (functionally) and I would still likely buy it again if my current one died out of warranty (can't beat $20) I'm getting concerned about the quality. review: excellent sunscreen with skin loving ingredients, broad spectrum, great little container. The "Drop the Bomb" BBOSONG Suns stick uses one of THEE best UVA/UVB sunscreen ingredients on the planet: "Bis-Ethylhexyloxyphenol Methoxyphenyl Triazine"! Say that 5 times fast. Or once. lol. It is a broad spectrum, highly photo stable, chemical sunscreen. Chemical sunscreens mean that they absorb rays and disperse as heat before they can reach skin and do damage. The SPF rating of 50+ and PA++++ means that it offers the highest amount of protection that a sunscreen can offer.  Korean skin care, particularly sunscreens, can use super effective ingredients that products made in (or for) USA can not have because the governing bodies have not approved it. It is not because they are unsafe, but because there is a significant amount of bureaucracy involved. No new sunscreen ingredients have been approved in the USA in over 15 years, sad since there are so many wonderful innovations in the rest of the world. We lag greatly behind. Fortunately, we can still buy these products.  The other sunscreen used in this product is, Ethylhexyl Methoxycinnamate (Octinoxate)- a less stellar chemical sunscreen that has mixed thoughts on its efficacy, safety, and desirability. It protects only against UVB rays and breaks down when exposed to light (10% per 30-40 minutes). However, when combined with another broad spectrum sunscreen, it compliments it very well.  The third sunscreen component is, Octocrylene.  Screens out the UVB and somewhat in the UVA II range. It is quite photostable (loses 10% of SPF protection in 95 mins) and is often used to stabilize other photo-unstable UV-filters (octinoxate) It is also often used to improve the water resistance of the products.  As for all the other ingredients- primarily stabilizers, viscosity controlling ingredients, hardeners-- basically all ingredients that make it a STICK than can glide onto the skin. It is formulated to melt into the skin on contact, and yet absorb thoroughly. Basically, you won't even know it is there.  And like so many other Korean skin care items, there are ingredients that go above and beyond the basic sunscreen-- included are skin loving ingredients (emollients, skin conditioners, soothers) such as Japanese knotweed, water lily, gotu kola (centella asiatica), camellia japonica, Lespedeza Capitata Extract (anti inflammatory), scutellaria (ie scullcap/mint), green tea, licorice, rosemary, chamomile  Has a super mild scent- clean, fresh almost like a deodorant, but subtle.  Happens to be a in a container that reminds me of deodorant. Super small, cute. Stick in a pocket or purse. I happen to love using it on my hands. I am in my 40s, and while I have been using SPF most of my life on my face, I figured it was high time to remember to put some on my hands. I like keeping this in my purse or my car, and applying it when I go to drive. That seems to be the time that my hands are most consistently exposed to the sun. Figure, hands on the steering wheel and in front of a big window. So yeh, this is perfect for that.  I have no problem using this on my face.  Doesn't grab skin when used over a moisturizer. If need be can be applied/emulsified in palms then patted on. I prefer it as my "reapply" SPF rather than my first application product (I am used to a cream style). When I do apply it to my face, I always run it over my lips. It is very silky, doesnt have a sunscreen flavor or feel, and it is adding much needed hydration and protection from the sun.   Again, I am in my 40s.. clear fair skin but with Rosacea (non acne- just redness and visible veins). Leans dry. Loves Korean skin care.  This is so clear, so clean feeling, and so incredibly light that I wish I could show you how it doesn't even feel like anything is on. Not greasy, not even dewy. My skin feels bare.  If I have any complaints, it is the use of fragrance. While it smells nice and doesn't really linger.. it would not make a top choice for use on my face. I do however like it for everywhere else and rather enjoy the light scent before it dissipates fully.  Even so, it is a really good product, so far. If I experience anything else, I will be back to say so.  For all the other ingredients, the each rate 1-2 (very low in terms of hazard to self or environment) on EWG Skin Deep Database

So, a couple of weeks ago I mixed up a capsule and applied it with the brush. I tried not to get any on my skin, but it was impossible. I let the dye cook for a couple of minutes and the thoroughly washed it off. It also easily came off my skin. Some of the gray hairs didn’t quite take, but the brows look completely natural. review: Formaldehyde?! Not safe. 2 Stars ⭐. After going over the ingredients in these products, the only two I would feel even remotely safe using would be this shampoo and conditioner. As a hair stylist, you do not want to use a product that contains formaldehyde and apply heat to it. You certainly do not want to use it every 6 weeks, as it's harmful to your health. It can cause breathing issues among other things. It's very hard to believe that I even saw actual formaldehyde on the back of this product, and so high up in the ingredients list. Even hair stylist must wear protective gear, such as gloves, aprons, masks, and be trained how to safely work with this hazardous chemical. Salons must have adequate ventilation and follow strict protocols regarding blow dryer temperatures and monitor formaldehyde levels at all times when they provide Keratin Treatments containing formaldehyde because of the immediate and long term health dangers.This is something you cannot possibly do at home. Also, the pretreatment that you add to the shampoo is extremely strong and stripping to your hair. When they say add just a little, no one knows what that means. That particular product, or the two main ingredients, should only be a small percentage of the product you're adding it to. I don't think you can mix this properly at home without causing damage to your hair and/or your skin. I "might" use the shampoo and conditioner, but I will not touch the pre-treatment nor will I touch the DIY home keratin treatment. Over the course of a few treatments, I can see this product going really awry for some people. They will end up with damaged hair and possibly other problems. It is not safe. I absolutely would not recommend it!

review: Nice look; feels pretty solid; but average in performance & value. This is a “dressed up” version of the Wahl “LifeProof” shaver (which I also reviewed). It has a more upscale look and feel to it, plus adds a battery gauge to show the charge level. However, the shave quality is the same – OK, but not a standout.  The case feels more solid than the LifeProof and, while it’s more of a traditional look, I think they did a nice job with the overall aesthetics. It is pretty grippy even with wet hands. It does not, however, feel as comfortable to hold as the more sculpted models such as most of the Panasonic shavers and some Braun shavers.  The shave quality of this model is identical to that of the LifeProof: very Remington in how it feels (close, but rather aggressive). Performance is best on the easy spots (cheek) but not as good on the more trickier spots (neck and jawline). The flex head helps with dealing with face contours but it lacks enough travel to do an excellent quality job.  The aggressiveness of the shave is dialed down when using it wet. It needs a very, very thin layer of shave cream (the gel style creams work well) or the head gets bogged down.  Love the trimmer! The positioning could be improved to make it easier to use, but it cuts very cleanly on sideburns and ‘shash trimming.  The controls are clean, easy to read and tell you all you need to know (charge and battery status).  I like the feel of this better than the Wahl LifeProof, but the shave quality keeps this at the same rating (average, which is 3 stars). It’s a very workable shaver, but for the price there are better choices available from Panasonic (anything in their Arc line) or, for less money, from Remington

review: Great combo of price, performance, and features. First let me say I don't have thick facial hair and can almost get away with shaving every other day.  My very first shaver was a Norelco -- since then I've tried razors (not worth the effort or cuts) and foil shavers (not a close shave and I have to go over areas, especially under the chin, over and over again).  Since I don't have to shave much, I didn't want to spend much on a shaver, so I tried a Braun 1775 and I just got tired of the noise, vibration, and rough shave.  Plus, the foil head is too delicate and gets damaged easily (I went through 2).  I decided to go back to a Norelco, did some research and found the 8160XLCC.  The price was reasonable and it had the features I wanted, especially the charge level indicator lights.  I've had it for a couple of months now and I really love it -- it gives me a quick, close, comfortable shave, it's quiet and has good battery life, and you can clean it by running it under the tap without taking anything apart. review: I wanted to like these soooo much…but nope, sorry. [[VIDEOID:dcc1995803f2ea0bca73889e0d891af]] I got the ikikin Soft Silicone Bath brush for two reasons:  1) replace my exfoliating face scrub and 2) replace my body wash pouff.  It sadly didn’t work for either purpose.  There are two sides on the brush:  one has little silicone fingers for regular exfoliation, and the other has…well, I don’t know what to call it.  The manufacturer says it has “short” bristles but it doesn’t.  They claim you can use it for deep exfoliation but I don’t see how.  It doesn’t have any holes on that side so the inside sponge can’t get any soap on to that side.  So it just kind of rubbed my skin raw because of the dryness…and not in a good way.  As for the side with the little silicone fingers…that does, indeed, have some holes to let the sponge inside squeeze the soap foam out.  But I had to really squeeze the brush several times to get anything out onto the surface of the brush…and then had to keep stopping and squeezing some more.  I also didn’t like the texture of the fingers.  It’s more of a rubbing feeling than an exfoliating feeling.  Way too rough on my face (and I use apricot scrub normally so I’m used to a lot of exfoliation).  And not flexible enough to go around the curves on the rest of my body.  As for the sponge inside…putting body wash on the outside as recommended means you waste a lot of body wash because it will run right off the silicone.  I squeezed my body wash onto the sponge itself on the inside, and that worked better…but as I mentioned before it still took a lot of squeezing after that to get the foam back out on the outside.  I also had hoped that I could put my little leftover slivers of bar soap in there and use those up…but squeezing the brush to get the foam started just broke up the slivers and didn’t do much else.  So no for me

review: Great for sensitive skin. I have extremely sensitive skin, and I generally have a hard time finding anything with sunscreen in it that doesn't burn my skin upon application or cause a rash.  Supergoop SPF 30+ doesn't irritate my skin, and I love that it doubles as a body lotion, since it saves me time in the morning.  It doesn't have a strong odor.  It's not greasy.  It works as a light lotion for your face under makeup.  This size is great for everyday use, especially in the summer.  Some reviewers mentioned taking this bottle with them on trips--honestly, I can't imagine this bottle would travel well, but the pump makes it easy for me to fill smaller travel-size bottles, so I can't say I have any complaints.  As an aside, I am not a chemist, but while in college I worked in a cosmetics department with a biochemist, and she told me that over time, physical sunscreens change their chemical composure -- they go through a chemical reaction that causes the sunscreen to go from UV-blocking to UV-absorbing, which is why there are use by dates on the bottles. review: Norelco Battery Replacement. I replaced the battery in my model 3605X, 14+ year old razor with this product. It has only been installed for about 3 weeks, but so far it performs flawlessly. All NiCd batteries loose their ability to recharge to full capacity over time, and my old battery would only stay charged enough to run the razor for about 3 hours. With the new battery, it works like it did when I bought it, with a full charge being held for a few days. However, you need to dispose of the old battery properly through recycling facilities, as it contains toxic cadmium. Unless you specifically need this battery for a Norelco razor, you might consider a different Sub 4/5 C battery with tabs, which is essentially what this battery is; the markings on this product do not resemble the original battery that I removed from my razor anyway. Note that replacing the battery with this product likely voids the razor's  warranty unless you are a qualified Norelco technician, and it is possible to break some tiny copper wires inside the razor during battery replacement, so do so at your own risk. You will also need a proper set of screw drivers, (3mm star bolt drivers in my case), and a soldering iron to replace the battery

review: Colored natural, kinky hair. I have bleached and colored natural, kinky hair. This is the first time I've ever colored my hair and I made sure to do my research on colored hair care, which includes protein treatments. Well, months had gone by and I still hadn't done a protein treatment. Madness, right? Eventually, the dyed parts (especially the ends) started to feel rough and dry.The ends were also knotting like crazy! I remembered a YouTube video I watched about hydrolyzed wheat protein. I ordered that and a pair of hair shears (prepared to do some clipping, which I had also been neglecting). I heard that you should expect to see results after the first use, but I was blown away! First, I cleansed my hair with shampoo. I didn't measure how much of the treatment I used but I mixed it in with my regular, wash out conditioner. After coating my hair in it, I covered my hair with a plastic cap then sat with my conditioning heat cap on my head for about 15 minutes.  My hair in general, not only the dyed area, feels softer and the colored ends feel smooth and manageable again. Also, waaaaay less knotting. After washing my hair, I put it in twists to dry. 2 days later I pulled out the twists to get a lovely, voluminous twist-out. Unfortunately, I didn't get the shears but Amazon promptly refunded me and I plan to reorder them shortly. I'm ashamed to say its been months since my ends have been clipped (which just compounded the problem) and I plan to use my protein treatment around once a month and trim when needed

I did get a minor rash after using for a week or so.  After reading a lot of the internet, I noticed three prevailing ideas.  1.  Allergic reaction. BIG DIFFERENCE.  2. Detox after using antiperspirant so long.  I did notice that my lymph nodes in my arm pits were tender which along with the rash seemed to fit.  They recommended dry brushing or massaging the area and time.  Massaging helped the lymph nodes calm down but did nothing for the rash.  3.  Friction burn.  Ding ding ding!! This is the winner! So, I started using tea tree oil as a primer during the day.  Like the first day, the rash was half the size.  I also discovered that not wearing the product to bed because I lay on my arms a lot and squish the pits causing friction rash.  So, baking soda free options at night.  Rash gone!  Hope this helps someone

review: Simply Brilliant. If we're completely honest, we've been conditioned by manufacturers these days to accept rubbish without complaint.  Quite true, you can dial into their computer and navigate circles around their voicemail system for a few hours until your anger dissipates.  Or is transferred to computer answering systems.  Whichever comes first.  Happily, however, such is not the case with the Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer.  Not only does this eager little trimmer solve several problems at once but it does so with a composure and aplomb that will sweep away the corporate fog and, suddenly, everything else you own will seem completely and utterly inadequate.  Trimming whiskers used to be such a chore that the ZZ Top look began to show some sense, if not appeal.  The constant recharging, sweeping up afterward, seemingly endless search for single-tasking components that had wandered off and an assembly/disassembly process for cleaning the tool that would make Bill Gates weep.  Philips, however, decided to go in a slightly different direction.  For a start, the battery holds on to a charge with a grip that would make Chuck Liddell cry. It doesn't last mere hours, days or weeks.  Under standard use, mine lasts well over a month.  Even when the battery light does begin to blink, what it really means to say is, "Pardon me but, at some point in the next several days, when it isn't too much of a bother, could you please plug me in for a bit?"  Nothing urgent about it whatsoever.  And once the lead is connected from socket to trimmer, a scant hour will have it fully refreshed and ready for another month on the road.  Then there is the all-in-one design.  Unlike most trimmers, which require that you dig around to find the correct attachment in order to trim your left eyebrow now that you're done with the right, nearly everything is built directly into this sleek little unit.  The only exception is a neat little detail trimmer that stands eternally at the ready in its own clear and obvious pocket inside the travel pouch.  That's it.  Nothing else to search out when you're dashing to work.  It's all right there.  Not everyone who sells a "vacuum trimmer" truly means it.  Most generate just a bit of wind, sufficient to scatter your whiskers over the widest possible surface.  I firmly believe my last vacuum trimmer was designed by a consortium of housekeepers seeking job security.  The T980, however, actually captures every single whisker, every single time.  And then there's a Turbo button that doubles the already adequate force of the vacuum's suction so that you can give yourself that wind-blown look if you so choose.  But, by far, my favorite thing about this trimmer is the way it feels.  It sits in your hand as if it were custom designed specifically for you.  It's lightweight and nimble around the bends, falls effortlessly into its case when deeds are done and assembles as if there is an invisible force guiding your hand at every step of the way.  I am genuinely amazed at the simplicity of removing and replacing the grille guard.  For a time, I thought it must be drawn together by magnets.  But it isn't.  It's just a set of exceptionally well designed tabs and slots that quickly correct a hurried approach and seat the grille home with a satisfying, subtle click.  Most products on the market today are slapdash clumps of flimsy plastics and mechanics that are carefully designed to fail at the worst possible time.  And, for some reason, we have accepted this corporate abuse in the hopes that prices would compensate us somehow.  But they don't really, do they?  When you've re-purchased the same device five times because it keeps breaking, whose interests are truly being served?  So, then, the T980 is a warning shot fired over the bow of companies everywhere who treat their clients like stupid, slobbering monkeys, devoid of choice or rights.  With it, Philips is saying, "See, everyone?  You needn't accept rubbish in exchange for your hard-earned money.  We've done it properly and at a price point that is competitive."  And why wouldn't we honor that?  I wish my hair grew faster

review: creamy semi matte finish, bold, bright pop of color, fades w/ drink & food, smudges. Not shiny, not matte, somewhere in between. They call it semi-matte, and I agree. But anyone who has lines or parched lips, should always avoid any formulation with the word "matte" in it. You are better off with a lip liner and a moisturizing lip gloss or lip stick. Matte will always dry down and make the lip skin pucker a little. My lips aren't wrinkled, but I can tell the formula pulls the skin together a little.   The color is bold. 06 Crush Berry appears to be a blue based red. Definitely red, like a classic red, just blue based rather than orange based. It feels super smooth on the lips, not at all tacky. Doesn't feel or look dry to start, but it dries down to a matte look. Can achieve a decent level of stain with a few applications and blotting.  The first pass has a more oily look and feel to it. I smash my lips one way, and it appears to come off lips a little. Then I smash them in the other direction, and the color is there again. But once it sets, it isnt budging like that again. Any color disappearance is from drinking, eating.  The case looks and feels good. The overall product is pretty good, just comes down to wanting a bold semi matte color that will perform like most other lipsticks- wears off with drinking & eating.Even then it doesnt disappear. Just might need to even out the color after awhile.  It seems to hold up to the product description. So for that (and all else), I give it a solid 4 stars.  I'm not in love with it, but it looks nice in pictures. Has a bright pop of color. This is not a subdued look at all. I find that it nearly matches a bold lip tint that I like by "I'm Meme"  https://www.amazon.com/dp/B091GSRN78/

review: Made an impressionable impact.. great for teen boys!. This was a lifesaver for our son with an acne issue! Being a 17yr. old boy who was feeling the high school inferiority angst at a time in life thats rough enough.. bc duh, it’s High School!! We ended at a dermatologist who gave us a regiment of: 1. wipe the counter clean of all gimmicks/products 2. use a dye/scent free soap and water x2 daily 3. follow up with clindamycin 1% to dab on larger   trouble spots ONLY..!! So, on our way to where we wanted to go... improvement was ours in leaps and bounds. Then, Covid... Then, the mask mandate!! Soon after we developed a sort of acne/rash on bridge of nose and around mouth 2” due to synthetic material where the mask touches the face. Dr. said mask was compromising the skins ability to breathe and would subside after mandate lifted. Only, attending school x5 days a week 100% fully masked- didn't give skin any reprieve and with no end in sight, I went seeking help for acne irritation.  As of now, we’re on the 25th day of Geologie’s 30 day regiment and I am so grateful we found this product. TBH, I personally didn't realize the extent of red, blotchy and puffiness this irritation had brought his poor skin.. until after using approx. 5 days- when we noticed a decrease in the puffy/red that had gradually appeared. Over the last 2wks- it has been clearing things up a little at a time and things seem less inflamed and aggravated. What I’m most impressed with- this hasn’t caused excess breakout like many other products in the past had done and I’m sure it’s bc, of the compound. Nor, has it left skin overly dry.. and both of these are huge!! I’m not even sure how it does it, maybe it’s witchcraft?! For comparison: a BFF uses Proactiv (as seen on TV!) with her 2 son’s for past x3 months and I’m actually surprised the results we had seem similar but, in a lot less time!? I applaud the packaging as it doesn’t have a feminine vibe, nothing “fu-fu-“ to turn teen boys away from using “girl stuff!” Trust me, I’ve gone this route before- and it does matter to some! A few suggestions I have: leave out on bathroom counter to remind one to use daily, use fresh pillowcase every few days to keep any excess bacteria away, wash mask daily if poss. while this mandate applies.. and most of all- keep your hands away! Easier for adults- harder for teens.  As with any product there are many factors to it success.. and for obvious reasons. review: Poor Overall Performance and Longevity. I bought this in July and began using it in early September.  It seemed like it would be easy to use, as well as clean and maintain.  The extra features included a beard trimmer, a nose-hair trimmer, and a face brush.  There was also a charging cord but no actual charger.  I ended up using this every day for about 100 days before the lid broke for the cutter housing.  It broke right where you would expect at the hinge after normal opening and closing for cleaning per the instructions.  For what I paid for the shaver, it didn't seem worth it to try and find a replacement cutter housing.  The shave itself is by far the worst I've ever gotten from an electric shaver.  I did use it consecutively for more than several weeks to allow my face to adjust.  This wasn't the issue as my face was already used to using electric shavers and I had no adjustment period issues with my face.  The issue was that the cutters were just plain dull and ineffective.  Even with three heads I would say I spent at least twice as long shaving with this shaver as compared to my last one.  Though it has three cutting heads, I would sometimes have to make a half a dozen passes over the same area before the stubble was cut flush with my skin.  The shaver seemed to use a lot of charge for a single shave.  Enough of a charge that it typically took 4+ hours to fully recharge after a single shave.  I'm not sure if it was the battery or the charging cord but the charger was actually the same one I used with the previous shaver with much better results.  The nose hair trimmer worked well.  I never used the beard trimmer or facial brush.  After cheaping out on this unit, I ended up buying a Panasonic Arc4 for 3 times more than what I spent for this one but so far it is absolutely worth the extra money.  Do yourself a favor and don't cheap out and buy this like I did

review: Great oral irrigator - read this for a list of the adaptor sizes. I purchased this SMAGREHO oral irrigator in March 2018.  The water diverter is metal, as is one of the adaptors.  The rest of the adaptors are white plastic.  All of the adaptors have male threads on both sides.  The threads on the diverter are female, and the threads in your faucet which your old aerator screwed in to need to be female as well.  The metal adaptor fit our old (1970's / 1980's) Moen faucets.  I measured the outside diameter of the threaded part of each of the adaptors - the part that screws into your faucet.  Here are the diameters: 0.68-0.69", 0.76-0.77", 0.83-0.84", 0.92" (this is the metal one), and 1.07-1.08".  The other side of each of the adaptors (the side that screws into the diverter) measures 0.83-0.84".  I am impressed by the high-quality silicone gaskets that came with the unit.  I experienced no leaks.  My faucets are the type where you pull the handle upward to turn it on.  This makes it tricky to precisely adjust the water pressure, so the pressure is high enough to wash out food particles, but not so high it is painful to use.  I suspect that facets which have handles that you rotate would give easier / more precise control of the water pressure

review: Very strong scent at first, but it disappears very quickly.. I really loved the idea of this Boiess Baby Cologne "Les Enfants" in White Blossom. Not because I think it is a good idea for a baby, because boy, is it not. I actually thought it would be perfect for myself since I don't like loud fragrances. The description of the scent profile really enticed me, as I love all of the notes. I was able to try both the Lavanda and the White Blossom scents. Both of the "Cologne" sprays smell identical to me. I can't say that I can tell them apart at all. They both have a very strong earthy, herbal, slightly floral scent that is heavily ladened with alcohol upon spraying. It stays very strong for several minutes, but then starts to dry down. Sadly, once it dries down, the scent pretty much dissipates. If I don't spray it heavily at first, which is too much for my asthma to handle, much less any baby, the scent just goes away completely. I must spray it on me again. If I spray it on a few times over an hour or so, I can smell the ever so slightest hint of it on my clothing later, if I put my nose right on it. That is a lot of spraying for very little payoff. I know this is meant for kids mostly, but I would think the scent would and should last longer. Sure, my grandsons will like using it, maybe or not, as it is quite strong at first. But, I think it would just be more for the fun of it and very short lived. This is also very expensive "Cologne" to not be able to smell it after 30 minutes, and right at $28 is too expensive for me to buy just for the fun of it.   For others this "Baby Cologne" may be something wonderful or maybe they can smell it more than I can. As I said, I really love the idea of a light fragrance, but not for babies. I do wish the scent stuck around more for me

review: This was a steal at this price!!. Eeeeeeekkk I'm so excited about this!! I love my Dry Bar Buttercup hair dryer, but really wanted a diffuser for it because I like to scrunch my hair time to time. When I added it to my cart, it was $21 I believe. That's still cheaper than Sephora so I was going to get it but waited. SO GLAD I DID. Randomly, it dropped to $12.12!!!! Purchased immediately!!  It fits my hair dryer perfectly. But, I can tell by looking at it that my hair dryer isn't a standard size on the end so I had to purchase the Bio Ionic brand since that's who makes my hair dryer. Worth it! It says universal, but I would still take measurements to make sure it'll fit yours if it isn't a Bio Ionic brand because they are not ever all universal.  The part that attaches to your hair dryer is not a hard plastic- it is rubbery (but firm) so it slides onto your hair dryer but doesn't "click" into place. I think that's why they say it's universal because this allows for some difference in the size of your dryer. But still do your research and compare your hair dryer to the size of the Buttercup hair dryer because it fits it perfectly.  You can also twist the diffuser to open up the vents or close them to control the air flow (see pictures). There will always be air flow on the outer ring of the diffuser, but you can completely close off the center, which is nice if you don't want a ton of force.  I love it and it was completely worth it!

I achieved this color by mixing equal amounts of Blue Mayhem and Pimpin Purple and then diluting the mixture with conditioner. I wrapped my head in saran wrap and a towel for about an hour, but unwrapped it halfway through to massage the mixture and redistribute the dye.  My hair felt really damaged after bleaching and sucked up the dye scary fast, but after rinsing and deep conditioning it felt soft and healthy again. I'll probably do a weekly deep condition with some dye mixed in to extend the life of the color

review: this is a medium tint- definitely gives sun kissed glow, absorbs well, hydrates, non greasy. Oops! I didn't realize when I ordered this that it says, "medium" in the product description, which is what I assume is the level of tint as this is a tad dark for my very fair skin. I don't see an option for any other tint level, so this might be it. Medium-- which appears rather dark and warm directly out from bottle, BUT after it is applied it seems to just blend in- albeit just a hint of color-- not opaque like a foundation. I am surprised it blended in as much as it does as my skin is quite fair & pink, with cool undertones. Still, I likely won't use this by itself. It blends in, but it gives me a slight tanned look, "a sun kissed glow".  Tells me that with sweat or uneven application I could have trouble with resulting look. My plan is to mix it in with one of my sunscreens that have a greater white cast..  This is a physical (ie mineral) sunscreen, using zinc oxide. Physical Sunscreens work by sitting on top of the skin to deflect and scatter damaging UV rays away from the skin (whereas chemical sunscreens absorb rays, converts them to heat, then releases). They are often referred to as physical blockers. The benefit of using zinc oxide is its strength in protecting your skin against the sun. It is one of the most effective sun protectors available, blocking out both short and long UVA rays and all UVB rays. Either type is great, and it depends on what works best with  your skin.  This product is rated as having a BROAD SPECTRUM sun protection factor of 31 (you want anything over 25). There are some other delicious, skin loving  ingredients contained in this product such as shea butter, jojoba, oilve oil, and vitamin e. It comes out thin, and applies smoothly. It provides a light sheen which you may or may not like. Not greasy. It absorbs well. I really like the multi action sunscreens. While I wear sunscreen all year round, and I have elaborate skin care routines.. I tend to keep it super simple in the summer. I tend to forgo my morning skin care ritual for just sunscreen (I figure I will be reapplying often, sweating it off, etc.. so why waste other skin care goodies when I can find a decent SPF product that will also moisturized my skin). So with this having ingredients that are good for my skin and help keep it moisturized, I feel better about keeping it so simple.  Again, I would like it better if the tint was a better match. That is on me that I didn't notice the "medium" in the description. And it also says that it gives skin a "sun kissed glow". If that is at all appealing to you, then give this a try. If your skin is anything darker or warmer than cool, fair skin.. then give this a try. There is NO WHITE cast, at all. If your skin is real oily, then this may be too much for you.. not sure. It feels goo on my normal to dry skin; seems to absorb. It doesn't feel heavy, and it doesn't feel like... sunscreen. It is light.  My skin: mid 40s, leans dry, semi sensitive, non-acne Rosacea (redness, visible veins), I avoid sun-- I always use SPF all year, and often wear a hat or visor. My favorite skin care is sunscreen. If I use nothing else, it is sunscreen that I keep in my routine. I go through a lot, and try a lot.. if I don't like it for my face & neck, then it gets used on rest of body. This is a new brand for me to try, and so far I like it (even though I have to tone it down by adding it to  one of my more white cast sunscreens.. OR go for the sun kissed glow).  I hope this helped . I will be back to update if I learn anything new, or think of anything else

review: A little pricy, but worth it -- the color and design are beautiful, and the barrette is great for thick hair. They don't pull or catch my hair, they don't stretch out of shape, they don't break and bend.  I know this is a lot of $$ to spend on a barrette when you can get one for a fraction of this price at your corner drug store, but these France Luxe barrettes are worth it.  This coral colored scallop design is beautiful, and the barrette hold a lot of hair.  This is definitely for thick hair.  France Luxe also makes boule style barrettes for fine hair -- so if you don't have a thick mop, I would check out the other France Luxe designs. review: Hmmmmm....Yes For the Cost. I am straddling the fence on this product.  I may be critiquing a bit harshly, considering that this is a drugstore product and the cost was minimum.  On one hand this is a surprising little gem for a high end makeup lover, such as myself.  Albeit, I expected the consistency to be a bit thicker, but it wears well without creasing and the applicator does not clog or get goopy as I expected. As a matter of fact, the thinner consistency became a bonus in the warmer months when I wear lighter textured foundation and less face powder. I cannot give it 5 stars, because the colors advertised in the photo is misleading. It shows 3 shades, but you actually receive 3 of the same shade. I ordered beige, but it is actually more of a pink shade.  I mixed in a couple shades of foundation and it became a usable shade.  Again, for the cost, this did not present a major problem.  However, if the pack contained 3 shades as shown, the buyer would be able to create their own shade of concealer.  Had I not had a few sample shades of foundation that I otherwise would not be able to use, the product would have been a waste.  I paid just shy of $10 for a package of three. review: Doesn't irritate my sensitive skin. Creamy,  requires very little to use. No actual change to wrinkles.. I'm not a big believer in all the hocus pocus claims made by every single women's skin care product on the market. They all say they will make your wrinkles or crows feet shrink or smooth out or give your 40 something face a "youthful" glow again. At best, these products moisturize, cleanse, and some provide some protection from sun exposure damage.   This serum from EB5 makes the usual claims, of course, but it's not as outrageously expensive as so many of the other brands. It's a creamy concoction and it takes very little to cover my entire face - the instructions say just use one pump and that is sufficient. There's a faint scent that makes me think of Asian food - I guess that's the sesame seed oil,but the scent fades quickly. It takes about ten minutes to fully absorb into my skin, so I am not using this immediately before going to bed. I haven't had any skin irritation or breaking out in a week. Nor have I noticed any visible difference in the overall condition of my skin and no "plumping" in my laugh lines. My face is soft and it feels just a moisturized as when I use only my regular moisturizer. So....four star rating for no negative reaction and for being a nice enough moisturizer requiring very little product

review: Very rich and moisturizing - thick cream. This is an interesting face mask. You get 5 masks for $20 so an ok price, maybe slightly more expensive than usual. You apply this mask to a clean face like you always do.  When you open the package you find 2 masks in it, they split the mask up into 2, the top and bottom.  This mask is the first cream mask I have ever used. You will first notice the pleasant scent, the reason I ordered this in the first place. I have a serum by Abib that I love and has an incredible fragrance so I figured this one has to be a great product. This mask feels kind of weird on your face because of the cream. It reminds me a bit of nivea cream to be honest, fragrance wise and thickness / consistency wise. So after the 20 minutes are up you take it off and realize there is still a lot of cream on your face. So you gently massage it into your skin. My face felt a bit sticky from all that extra cream to be honest. After about 20 minutes or so that feeling did start to fade, that is just how long it took for all of it to absorb. This is one rich cream I tell you.  My face was nicely moisturized though and it definitely had a bit of a glow from all that cream to it to be honest.  All in all this is a nice mask, but maybe a bit too rich for me. I think this would do wonders when your skin is super dry, like on a horrible winter day when you have been outside in the wind all day and your skin is almost peeling off from the cold dry wind. I’m not sure why sodium bicarbonate (baking soda) would need to be added to the organic aloe leaf juice. The product description mentions “we perfected our serum by enriching with Vitamin E, & Citric Acid for improved nutrient absorption.” I don’t see Vitamin E listed in the ingredients. It doesn't evaporate like my acetone does, so a little goes a long way.  Instead of using it as directed (applying directly to the nail with the included dropper), I applied a half dropperful onto half a cotton ball. Then I applied the cotton ball to my nail and let is set about a minute. Then I rubbed the polish away as I would with acetone. Pure Body Naturals Nail Polish Remover takes a little longer than acetone to remove the polish but it is faster than the non-acetone polish remover purchased from a store. Best of all, since it doesn't evaporate, that half cotton ball lasted for all ten nails. My nails had a minimum of a high-adhesion base coat, two coats of nail polish, a holographic top coat, and a quick dry top coat (5 coats total). Four accent nails also had nail polish nail art designs that added another coat of polish (6 coats total). This product removed everything cleanly, with no trouble, very little time, and my nails felt amazing.  The bottle is 4 ounces, doesn't evaporate as I'm using it, and requires a small amount of product, I am confident that I am getting a good deal. Since it's all natural and non-chemical, those who are concerned about what they're saturating their nails and the surrounding skin with can put those worries aside. review: Works on every level.... So, for a man who thinks his looks strike a resemblance to that of Anderson Cooper.. (bc, of the devilishly handsome silver fox short crew cut) mixed with a longer (3/4”) faux-hawk frontal vibe.. this is a great product to work with this style as it complements the cut really well! As one who’s always used hair gel (daily x30+ yrs!) it’s hard to find one we have not tried. Bold Men casual- sold just under $20 for 3.3oz. Is a higher price point so, the expectations were high and happy to say, this came through impressively.  This gel has an ability to last thru the day without becoming razor sharp quills nor, a crusty-crumbly flake after a full day of wear in tear. Being one who prefers a touchable hold (the hardest combo to find btw!!) this gives that to you.. We found, unlike cheaper store bought brands- less is more! (too much will weigh down the hair) **A trick of the trade for any who want to accomplish short spikes- use less product!!  Best results came from using no more than  a nickel size amount onto towel (50%) dried hair.. and finger combing into place. The hold stays movably put.. performing better then ever expected- yay!! TBH, this may take getting used too.. IF, you’re norm is the “frozen gel look!” Hack: one can finger style hair into place with this- then, use blow dryer on a lower setting for just a moment.. it will expedite the setting process- giving specific direction to the final look. (A convertible would do the same but.. not sure It’s feasible in winter ha ha!)  Product is thick yet, offers just enough slip to give you pliability to style before it settles. Note: color is clear… It’s just the container that is black! After hair is set, this absorbs vs. shellacs to the hair- letting hair have movement and touchable texture.. The scent is nice with a masculine appeal And after 3wks. of daily application we’ve used approx. a tad over 1/4 of content (to give you an idea how long it will last..) thus far, washing daily we’ve noticed no unwanted build up.. which is also a big deal- as this can lead to flakes/Dandruff..!! A good shampoo scrub removes product easily enough.. and paired with daily conditioner, it’s not over-drying to the hair. Making the $ seem worth all the quality benefits.  This is a top quality higher end product that best fits those who have a moveable set style they like their hair to maintain throughout the day.. this can achieve the desired look and look fantastic- and does so, without all the unwanted side effects that can come with daily use of hair gel.. I hope this info can help your decision… Feel free to let me know!

review: For medium to thin hair. Handle and paddle is very sturdy. The bristles not so much. I have thick curly hair and just got tired of using Combs. I also wanted to invest into a quality wooden brush to cut my scalp massages in half. This brush isn't for you if you have thick curly hair like mine. The little bulb tips tend to snag on my curls and I can hear my ends ripping and breaking. Mind you, this was me brushing as gentle as possible with added help of oil and detangler for slip. I bought another Wet Brush for the days when I want to brush wet. And honestly the wet brush was way better quality, id give it ten stars if I could. I've never had an easier combing experience than what I've had with my wet brush. It's just slips through my hair. Well to the get to the point I think the wooden brushes without the bulb ends are better for detangling. I also want to mention that these are supposed to be wooden bristles but they must be made from different wood because they broke very easily whilst combing. And also many came loose, I know I have very textured coarse hair but I think if the bristled weren't bulbed this might not have been the case. If you have straight to wavy, thin to medium texture, this might be for you though. It's well made, but just not made for the kind of endurance my hair demands unfortunately. I will be buying better quality in the future, in this case paying extra is worth it if you got my kinda hair. Just go for a sturdy European made wooden brush. If any one is curious about the wet brush it's ranges between 5-8$ I highly recommend. 😊

review: Gran afeitadora !!. Tras 15 años de fieles y diarios servicios, decidí reemplazar mi antigua Philishave 715. Es liviana, silenciosa y de fácil manejo. Buena duración de la batería. Puede usarse con o sin el cable de conexión eléctrica.  CONS:  Creo que el diseño del sistema de recarga debe pensarse mejor:  1) Tanto la plataforma como el mecanismo mediante el cual se apoya la máquina en dicha plataforma no parecen muy resistentes.  2) Para un funcionamiento más inteligente, la recarga debería funcionar automáticamente al detectar que la batería llega a un nivel bajo de carga. Así se podría tener la plataforma conectada permanentemente al enchufe y colocar siempre la afeitadora en su plataforma cuando no está en uso. Actualmente, y por sugerencia del fabricante, es el usuario el que debe administrar el proceso de recarga "cuando la batería esta cerca de agotarse".¡¡Solo que el equipo no tiene ningún indicador para saber el estado de carga de la bateria y, por lo general, simplemente nos enteramos porque la afeitadora se detiene en medio de una afeitada !!

In the pictures im comparing them to long coffin nails and xxxl nails. You can definitely see the difference between the long and xxl but no big difference between the xxl and xxxl. They do have a curve. They are thick on the tips the nail area is a little more flexible but I use the Modelones 4 in 1gel nail glue and they hold pretty good. They are easy to cut and file. review: Did not work for me. Let me begin this review by stating that I have been using Egyptian, Indian and Pakistani 100% henna for over 30 years with beautiful results that lasted a full 3 months.  I decided to try this product because I wanted a change from all the red highlights and thought it would be nice to tone down to a browner hue. So in addition to the hassle, mess and expense of doing this treatment (and make no mistake - it's messy and time consuming) I will have to double up this month and do my regular henna only routine.  I did a bit of research, by the way, and learned that most henna/indigo distributors, unlike Harvest Moon, suggest mixing up the henna and indigo powders SEPARATELY and then combining.  Based on my experience, I'd have to say this would probably work better (the rationale probably being the same as why combining shampoo and conditioner together don't work as well as shampooing and THEN conditioning).  Likewise, everyone else except Harvest Moon recommends wrapping the hair in plastic wrap and then covering with a shower cap and leaving on for a MINIMUM of 2 hours (Harvest Moon says their product works in less than one hour and is against wrapping.) review: I LOVE this Little Machine!. I have over 200 bottles of regular nail polish, more than 30 gel polishes and about 40 stamping polishes. review: Time to put the razor away!. I [RECOMMEND] this roll on wax kit. First time user who is happily throwing away her razor!  Pros: ~Reasonably priced ~Easy to find refills ~Easy to use (once you get the swing of it)  Cons: ~On/off button and temp buttons in the way while using ~Corded - limits mobility  If you still want some more information about this product, please read on! ______________________________________________________________  I was a little apprehensive to use an at-home wax kit. Other than my eyebrows, I have no familiarity with waxing, either in a salon or at home. I was slightly disappointed that the instructions were not clearer for a beginner. My biggest issue is when loading the honey wax - does the lid stay on? Does the tape stay on? I'm still not sure. I loaded it with the lid and tape on and it heated up just fine. The wax cartridge is reusable (unless you use all the wax in one sitting) so I assume you take the lid and tape off, as it is off when you go to reheat and reuse.  There is a temperature range that goes up to 125 degrees (f).  I was not sure where the temp should be or where my personal heat threshold would be. I set it to 100 degrees (f) and it seemed to do the job. I will probably go hotter the next time around. The wax rolls on nice and easy, the waxing strip is easy to get on and get off. It also comes with 10 finishing wipes, but they did not seem to do anything for me.  A couple small issues came up while I was doing this. First, the machine is corded. Not the end of the world, but it does limit where you can do this. Second, the operation buttons are in the middle of the machine. Several times I turned the machine off or lowered the temperature while rolling on my leg. It could be a me thing, and didn't really interrupt the process, just a small issue to note.  I tested the wax on my wrist (like you would a baby bottle), and didn't know how to get the wax off after. The finishing wipe didn't work, soap and water didn't work.  I used some isopropyl alcohol and a cotton ball to finally get it off. I suppose you could use a wax strip to get it off too, but didn't think off that at the time. Overall, this was a good experience and a great alternative to shaving

review: Charging plug won't stay in.. I have previously reviewed the 7181 model very positively.  These two models are exactly identical, with the only difference being the 'Spa' in the title and the rotating brush head attachment.  I am not re-reviewing the actual epilator because it is the exact same model.  I will re-post my original favorable review of that unit below after I have reviewed the changes in this Spa unit.  What's Different: The word Spa on the packaging and the rotating brush head attachment that is supposed to smooth skin.  That is all!  Do I feel it is worth the extra bump in dollars?  No.  If you are the type that needs to have all the bells and whistles even though you will probably never use them after the first time, then go ahead; but if you are frugal and would rather exfoliate and smooth skin with a good wash and exfoliating gloves, them save the extra money and have a nice night of take-out.  I have found the brush attachment to not sting when my legs are dry but sting and be extremely sensitive in the shower.  The brush actually feels stiffer when I use it during showering.  I have used the brush before and after epilating to the same end results.  I still have a lot of dry/dead skin and itchy legs.  I am still suffering from ingrown hairs and am hoping that if I continue to use the brush it will help me get on top of the dry skin issue.  Putting this brush to your face is not the most pleasant experience and I do not recommend it.  The bristles are just too stiff for that sort of application/use.  Using on other parts like your arms, feet and heels seems to be fine.  I did find that the stiffness of the bristles actually smoothed not only the balls of my feet but also heels.  Finally, I also used it on my shoulder and upper back area.  I really do wish that Braun would ship this model with a smaller attachment for face applications, considering that the price jumps considerably.  Included is a small 1 1/2 inch straight brush that can be used to 'brush' away the hairs from the pivoting roller head and mechanism.  I implore Braun to hear my request and follow through with shipping a brush with longer and stiffer bristles that will not bend and collapse while attempting to brush away hairs.  MAJOR ISSUE and CON:  I have checked a few other reviews and find no complaints regarding the charging cord that supplies power to the unit.  From the moment that I unboxed the item, the charger continuously pops out!  C.O.N.S.T.A.N.T.L.Y.  As annoying as that was to type out, it is much more annoying to have to constantly replace the plug.  It does not stay in and is a very loose fit.  I am not sure if the unit that shipped was defective in this matter or not.  Forget walking by this thing... it will pop out.  Opening a drawer that this unit is resting on... pops out.  Look at it the wrong way... it pops out.  You can hold the unit in your hand while placing the charger and it will surely pop out.  I have lost precious charging hours because of this issue.  Highly recommend this epilator and the model 7181 that was previously reviewed.  I just cannot justify spending so much more for a mere brush exfoliating attachment that cannot be used everywhere.  The charging cord lost the second star for me.  If you are in the market for a great epilator, then you have found one; just be aware that the more expensive choice is not always the best in this case.  Here is my original review for the 7181:  Both are identical in style, shape, color and mechanics. Ok... so those were not the exact expletives that were used at that very first moment. I have never used an epilator. This is my personal experience as an Epilating Virgin. I suffer from ingrown hairs on the outer part of my lower legs (below knee). I carefully unpacked the package, Braun epilation wipes, read the instructions/care manual and charged my new device for a bit. I couldn't wait for too long so I cleaned my legs with the wipe. The wipe does nothing but clean your legs and make them smell great. Seems a very 'placeboish' product. I read up on online forums and took pain killers because it would supposedly reduce inflammation and pain later on. Now onto the epilating...  The sound when turned on is very nerve-wracking even on it's low setting or as I refer to it as, "chicken speed". It made me nervous and a bit uneasy, but I still braved on! OH MY!! Add a few expletives and constant, OUCHES, OH MY GOD, HOLY HELL and so on and you get my point. The kids came to my bedroom because they heard the commotion. Trying to describe it, I would say it feels like lightening rods. I believe that sensation is translating that way because you are tweezing 40 hairs at the same time. When you tweeze one leg hair you feel that momentary Peter Griffin moment of, "Ahh SSSSS Ahh SSS". Multiply that by 40 times; hence my swearing as if I was being tazered. So there I was and five minutes later I was epilating up and down my leg like a pro and even going into the top speed. It no longer hurt! Who would have thought that the pain would subside? Rather that you could get used to that sensation. I moved to my knee and the pain came rushing back; knees are painful and continue to be!  My experience: Initially I was nervous, just from the sound of the whirring. I am so happy that I went through with it. Excitedly I looked at the calendar so that I could put into my review the exact number of days between epilation. I lost my epilator virginity on June 9th, 2012. Today is June 20th, 2012 and I have not epilated nor shaved my legs since that day. How do they feel? They feel like day number 3-4 after shaving (depending on how quickly your hair grows). This is insane and I only wish that I could have discovered this product sooner. I have stocked up on the Braun wipes even though I believe they didn't do anything. Today I used it in the shower on my underarms. The pain was excruciating and I had a dot of blood without it catching the hair. I immediately stopped. It wasn't worth it and I am not sure if the water makes it more difficult for the hair to be caught. The underarms will remain a strictly shaving region; as much as I loathe it.  Hair type/Skin color I am Caucasian and have very very fair skin that bruises easily. Waxing leaves me red for two days but the epilation went smoothly without any snags. A couple of hours later and my legs were not red and there were not any scabs. It does not help with the ingrown hairs and I have to still manually remove them. This has me motivated to pick up my exfoliation so that I could get to the bottom of those pesky ingrown hairs.  Highly recommend and suggest sticking past the first few minutes. review: Good for a gentle exfoliation or those with already good skin.. If you need a mild chemical exfoliant and want to cut out products from your routine, this might be the serum for you. It's a weaker concentration of retinol but with that trade, you get a less harsh serum that still keeps your skin hydrated and has a lesser chance of causing irritation. You can most likely use this as a serum/cream combo. Likely a big bonus for those with sensitive skin.  I've taken a break from my usual Tretinoin cream due to the extreme sun in my area but I do still need to keep up with chemical exfoliants and retinol has the added bonus of fighting acne like Tret does. My skin is definitely smoothing out again and looks more even, but it's a very very subtle improvement so I'm not sure if those that have significant texture issues or need a lot of brightening or fading will be pleased with this as it most likely would take a while to see visible results.  It's not a bad product but with such a low retinol percentage it is quite expensive compared to other retinol serums/creams on the market and also comes in a small bottle. review: So far this is working well for my sensitive skin; will see how it goes in the long run. First off, I have extremely sensitive skin overall, but especially on my face. To that end, I must be very carefully about what I put on. I do tend towards lighter or no scents, but have found some that work alright for me. But with or without scent, I can still have issues.
