I use a derma roller a couple times a week to help with hair in my beard and front of my head. At this point I then add a beard oil to these locations to help stimulate growth. Without doing major testing with all the elements, like a control group (area) of my head, it’s hard to say what works and what doesn’t. I feel like the derma roller has a large part in how well growth or at least slowing of loss goes. But, I have also come to believe some of these oils available do play a supportive role. review: Lavender Wow!. I've always wanted a plethora of the lovely boutique gifts that I usually can't afford, so I decided to try making some myself!  I used New York BioIogy 100% Pure & Natural Lavender Essential Oil to make some Lavender Bath Salts.  I googled to find a free recipe and just needed epsom salts, sea salt, food coloring and a small decorative jar (you can buy the kind of jar I used at a good craft store), and of course, the Lavender Essential Oil, which New York Biology sells for a very affordable price here on Amazon.  It was so easy to make the bath salts, and within mere moments of opening the bottle of essential oil and adding just a few small drops of it to my mixture of salts, my kitchen smelled like a lovely lavender sachet!  As soon as I can get the kids to sleep, I'll be having a nice, long, uninterrupted soak with this!  I used 1/8 cup Epsom Salt and 1/16 cup Sea Salt, 3 drops Lavender Essential Oil, several drops of red and blue food coloring, and then mixed it well. Then I spooned it into the jar and applied a cute little label with a gluestick! That’s all there is to it! (Some recipes I found used baking soda or baking powder, however it's been reported that if the mixture isn't COMPLETELY dry, the baking soda/powder will cause the jar to explode, so I left that part out of the mix.)  It smelled so good!  I’m thinking about also mixing this with some coconut oil (as a carrier oil, because you shouldn't use essential oils undiluted on your skin!) as a lovely lotion for the inevitable winter-roughened skin I get every winter!  Unlike some other Lavender Essential Oil brands I’ve used in the past, New York Biology’s Lavender Essential Oil’s scent lingered for quite awhile, which I was very pleased about. Other oils I’ve tried in the past dissipated too soon, but this was not the case with this oil.  I'm planning on making a lot of the Lavender Bath Salts with this oil and use them as stocking stuffers for Christmas!  *DISCLAIMER: I was offered a complimentary bottle of this Essential Oil to facilitate my review. review: excellent ingredients, could use more packaging info, works well w/ shamp & conditioner. I like the shampoo and conditioner a lot- leaves my hair soft, manageable, and healthy looking. I added in this serum as I hoped to gain hair density or at least reduce loss (or reduce cycle frequency and/or duration). I dont have trouble growing my hair, I have trouble keeping it. So my hair is long, but much less dense than previous years. I transitioned from minoxidil to this. I wont do that again, as any gains I got from minoxidil were lost-- and I do contribute some of that to not using this as consistently as I did that. I'll explain what went into that below. This serum helped the condition of my hair and scalp, so I think it works well with minoxidil instead of in lieu of it. I likely wont continue with the serum for a few reasons.  1. there was no instruction as to how to use this product. It is a dropper bottle, and I pretty much just used it like I did with minoxidil-- massaged whatever I pulled with dropper and distributed all over scalp, primarily at crown. Was this the correct way to do it? no idea. *  2. It does say to apply to clean hair. Well, many of us do not wash our hair every single day. I have long curly hair that leans dry and there is no need to wash it daily. So I am either applying this to unwashed scalp daily or it only gets applied a few times a week.  Hence the lack of consistency. So right here it eliminates some would-be users if it has to be on a fresh washed scalp.  3. the dropper is uncomfortable. I do not want to drop it from the dropper. I want to run it across the scalp so as to keep it from getting on my hair. The dropper is a little sharp feeling (at least my bottle that I received). I like the dropper style, and my thought is that if I were to buy this again, I would use a dropper from an old minoxidil bottle instead.  4. How long should this bottle last? Since I had no idea how much I should use, I often wondered if I used too much or too little. Any new hair treatment needs to be given 4-6 months of consistent use to see results, if any. I know the shampoo and conditioner helped, and this serum has great ingredients that will help existing hair and scalp health.. but the inconsistency on my part from lack of instructions as well as expectation of using on fresh washed hair made it impossible to see if I could get benefit from it.   * "It is best applied to damp hair after showering. We recommend visually splitting your scalp into 4 sections/quadrants. Depending on the amount of hair, use around 3-5 drops per quadrant. I like to drop into fingers and work into scalp. The remaining amount on your fingers you can work through your hair. It is perfectly fine to use the serum many times a day. That being said, it is important that the scalp/hair is clean" (--I saw this written in the community question section of this page. Including this on box or in a leaflet would have been greatly helpful)  The ingredients are of quality, the products work well together. I have since gone back to minoxidil, and once I have stopped the current shedding phase, I may buy another bottle to use as a support product. For that, I give it 4 stars

review: A great combo of sharp, smooth, and longevity. First off, let me say that I did not buy it here at Amazon, but locally here in singapore.  Exceptional, is what i would call it.  I'm certainly impressed.  To-date, i've used Gillette Platinums (blue,white box), Gillette 7 o'clock Super Platinums (black packs), Gillette 7 o'clock Super Stainless, Voskhod,  Astra SP, Concord, Croma, amongst a few others.  I would place the Gillette 7 o'clock Permasharps at the same top tier with Gillette 7 o'clock Super Platinum (indian), and the Gillette Platinum (russian).  But any blade, like a woman, needs the right approach to bring out her/its best.  Hence, i'll describe my shaving regimen. (a better regimen might bring out even more from this blade perhaps.)  1. I always have a hot shower before shaving, thus bringing out the hairs more. 2. I use the Rex Ambassador safety razor at a (extremely mild) setting of 1, thus contributing to the smoothness of the shave. 3. I use a combination of shower soap (bar) with sunflower oil (cooking), hand-lathered till the lather is thin but dense, not watery.  No brushes, shaving creams, shaving soap, scuttles, etc....completely unnecessary. 4.  I only go with-the-grain except for my neck. (which would certainly contribute to the longevity of the blade).  My stubble is hard and wiry and i do daily face and head-shaves.  I also do a once-weekly body shave, and a daily front shave from chest to netherregions.  After the shave, i pat-dry the blade with a microfibre cloth, and then strop it against the cloth on all 4 sides a couple of times each.  Ranking _______  Sharpness - 1. G 7oc Sp 2. G 7oc Permasharp tied with Gillette Platinum  Smoothness - 1. G Permasharp (gets smoother on 2nd and 3rd day) tied with G Platinum 2. G Super Platinum  Longevity (for both head and face-shaves in terms of days) - 1. G 7oc Permasharp - 8 and counting 2. G 7oc SP - 8 3. G platinum - 6-7  I judge the blade's longevity in terms of the degree to which i can get a clean shave with a single swipe.  I always do a 2nd swipe just to get any tiny stubble that might be left behind, but the first swipe must perform at 95%.  So when i say that a blade lasts for 6 days, i mean that i get 95% only after 2 swipes and not 1.  So, in sum, i definitely recommend this blade.  I just picked up 300 yesterday, and will pick up more up to a thousand the next time i go to the shop where i get it from here in singapore.  (cost : $9.00 sgd per 100 blades here.)

review: Finally eyebrows all day!. After a mountain of research on Wunderbrow products, I came across all of the recommendations for Blissful Brows and the Duo Eyebrow brush by Keshia to make it work. I couldn’t agree more! I have never been much of a makeup person and was a bit intimidated with semi-permanent makeup since it is prone to sticking on your face for a few days. With sparse eyebrows, at best, I needed makeup and a tool that I could manage as a novice (in my 50’s!) without looking like I had small animals resting on my forehead. This makeup and the Duo brush absolutely make it work! While my first instinct was “why do I need another makeup brush - this looks just like a lip brush?,” know that this brush is different and the Blissful Brows spoolie is prone to putting the makeup on too thickly. This Duo brush is also stiffer which controls the amount of makeup you have to use and is just perfect for making short angled strokes to mimic eyebrow hair. It also has a long enough handle so that a novice like me can manage to brush a straight and not to wide line for my eyebrow tails. I can make the line thick enough to avoid looking like I used a pencil on my face. If you do use Blissful Brows, I also recommend that you use the Duo brush firmly enough so that you are reaching your skin and not just touch up the tips of your brow hairs. If you stroke the Blissful Brows onto you skin and let it sit a minute or two to dry a bit, you will be able to use the Duo spoolie end to brush through your brows to create a more natural look so that your brows don’t look plastered on. The Duo brush holds a deceptively large amount of product - if you clean off the brush afterwards by squeezing it with a paper towel, you will be surprised at how much makeup is left over! Last thoughts: I find that if you wash your face with Noxema or if you use cocoa butter on your face as a moisturizer, you can get most if not all of the Blissful Brows off at the end of a long day (it stays put otherwise especially if you touch up your brows with toner before you apply Blissful Brows). review: Good.  However, probably not for oily skin. This foundation has potential IF you use a good primer with it.  I have combination skin and, like many foundations, this can settle into pores and creases.  Some foundations are better than others in terms of this tendency, and I'd say this one is about "par for the course" with regard to settling in pores and creases.  Primer will help.  This does seem to have a lot of moisture in it (as I've found with many foundations that have "satin" in the title).  For me, I feel a bit dewy and not quite clean enough in this -- especially when I look in my 10X magnification mirror.  However, I'd venture to guess that people with dry skin might actually appreciate this.  Whereas people with oil prone skin and/or visible pores -- will NOT appreciate this so much.  I ordered the Fair color and I'm an NC20 or NC25.  The color is great (not orange and not pink).  Nice neutral color.  It was just slightly lighter than my natural skin color and looked great with a light dusting of bronzer / blush.  I always prefer to err lighter than my natural color than to go to darker, and end up looking like and orange pumpkin.  NOTE  >>>Be sure to shake this well before each use<<<  I noticed if I don't shake this, the first spray is mostly moisture and has a shiny greasy effect.  Product applies much better if it is well shaken first.  This should be in bold print on the front of the can.  I spray this into a little eyelash tray (or back of hand, or where ever) and dab my make-up brush into it.  Then, apply to face.  Its a good foundation.  However, getting up into this price point, I felt some of the above minor gripes warranted removing a star

The device control is auto set at 30 minutes, upon plug in, but the ad (which I just looked at again) mentions 10 to 20 minutes a couple/few times per week. I know that red light therapy is now touted as a good thing, but I am afraid that if the instructions are not good and thorough then it could also pose some dangers. I only gave it 4 stars, because the conditioner that is automatically loaded into the razor during the charge, doesn't last long at all.  One reviewer wrote that he uses regular shave gel. Just rinse it off the shaver during shaving and after you finish, while the power is on. Since this shaver is made to use in the shower, using regular shave cream and rinsing the shaver doesn't cause any problem.  Given the price of razor blades, it won't bother me to spend $30 for replacement blades when needed.  I love this shaver, and feel badly that I couldn't give it 5 stars.  Buy the shaver, then using the much cheaper gel that you slap on your face

review: The good - it worked and my visual-contrast sensitive self can’t .... The good - it worked and my visual-contrast sensitive self can’t tell the difference from the OEM. So it’s a functional option.  The bad - this was my first screen replacement. It is daunting. The icracked video on YouTube was the most helpful (I may have watched all of the 6-Plus replacement vids). If you aren’t at least moderately experienced with gadget assembly and futzing, probably worth paying someone $100 or so to do it for you.  If you proceed, here’s what sucks about this product. The tri-wing driver IS garbage. I read this in the reviews before buying but I was raised by an electrical engineer and figured these were novices who didn’t have the finesse or small motor skills to work the driver right. Nope. I got to the home button (about 10 screws into disassembly) and the driver stripped out. I ordered a better driver set on amazon ($12 or thereabouts) and proceeded with those. Thus, this project ended up taking several days. I also bought a magnetic tack project mat (also on amazon, $12) which I would strongly recommend for keeping your TEENY TINY screws organized for reasssembly. Also suggest you take pics at every stage of disassembly because you may not recallhow they came apart. Especially if you’re waiting days for your new tri-wing driver to complete the job.  Also there is a proximity sensors filter that is a tiny white square of plastic/fabric inside the old screen. This is not included with the new screen. It is not entirely clear how to remove and transfer the filter to the new screen. In all the videos, the new screen already had that installed. I ended up breaking the old screen into tiny piece to get it out. Probably an exacto blade would get it. But you may want to buy a screen that already has this and forego the extra futzing.  I dropped one star for each of those issues. But the phone reassembled looked brand new and everything worked as it should. So it’s a viable option. Probably just not the best option. Good luck!

review: TL;DR Not worth hassle, better off with glue ons. Bought these as a test to see if the magnetic eyelashes are worth it. I’d never tried them before and figured, what the hell. As a long time eyelash fan, I completely understand the idea of spending hours on make up just to have that final step of putting glue-on lashes ruin it all, they’re not easy... so the appeal was here to give this new way a try.  Let me be frank, they’re terrible and not worth the money. I’ll take my chances on the glue...  To explain why... I can’t speak to all brands but the magnetic eyeliner for this has not been perfected yet. Despite shaking the container vigorously for 10-20 shakes per instructions, the eyeliner is thick. Even using my tiny regular eyeliner brush to apply I still ended up with thick raccoon lines. Fine, a night out it might be a little thicker than normal... I looked past it... however when it came to putting the lashes on...  They provided a metal applicator?! Why? The eyelashes stuck to it and make applying it to the eyeliner difficult. I switched to a plastic applicator  that I get from my regular glue on lashes. That made it a little easier. However, you have to be excessively careful not to get the eyeliner on your actual eyelashes or it will stick to them.  Okay, second try, reapply trying to make the eyeliner thinner and avoiding my eyelashes, waiting a little while for the eyeliner to fully dry, bam they stick! However, they’re a little higher than my lash line so I go to adjust them, the eyeliner flakes off and there’s a chunk of eyeliner missing (it’s attached to the magnet of course.) I take my small eyeliner brush, fill in the hole, wait for it to dry and place it right back.  They’re on, they look decent (albeit thicker eyeliner than usual even for a night out) however I can’t apply any mascara to make them blend with my natural eyelashes (or they move and I do the patch job all over again) and I feel as though one swift gust of wind and they’ll be out of alignment.  There’s a few reviews here with people who have had success and if that works for them that’s great, I will be going back to my regular glue on eyelashes. It takes practice, I’m sure, just like regular glue on eyelashes but if the convenience isn’t there why would I buy them over glue ons?

review: Great hair cutter, easy to use.. My wife is a professional hair stylist. She cuts my hair every 2-3 weeks and relies heavily on using electric shears to do so.  This unit works very well. It can work plugged in, or with battery, which should give you about 40 minutes of time per charge.  The shears are sharp and do a great job of cutting through my thick hair. The attachments are also very nice. Unlike other units that have 6 or 7 different guards depending on what you want to do. It has a fixed length one, a short variable one, and a long variable one. For my hair she used the short variable one.  The settings go from 1/16 of a inch up to about 3/4 inch, and the long variable one goes up from there.  Having the variable length guards is great as it reduces the number of guards you need and allows you to change lengths on the fly.  Using the shears without the guard is also good for trimming to the skinline, edging and shaping.  The only complaint my wife had is that she wishes it were a little more powerful on battery, but wasn't really lacking in power, it is just that she usually uses professional shears. Being fairly handy taking and reassembling gadgets, I took it apart to inspect the motor.  When I took the bottom seal off the motor, it was full of "gunk" (no other way to describe it).  I cleaned the bottom seal and what I could inside the motor compartment (could not remove the motor).  Then I had to take the seal for the pump mechanism off and started to rotate the gear on the motor shaft (with the power off) to loosen the shaft (which appear to be jammed).  I turned the power on and continued to move the gear and shaft until the motor began to turn on its own.  I then blasted the motor compartment with WD40 and the motor spun flawlessly.  Left the device disassembled all day (to let it thoroughly dry out), reassembled and it worked like a champ. review: A Surprising Find. I got this today and tried it out right away. I only had a couple minutes and was happy to discover it blends quickly and easily. I’m fussy about makeup and don’t like the look of anything too obvious. After initial application I used my hands to gently wipe away excess and help it melt into the skin, it made a big difference. As an aside, it was very difficult to wash off my hands so I suspect it won’t transfer all over the place. It lives up to its name and imparts a lovely glow but doesn’t look oily or greasy. So far I’ve had it on for five hours and it still looks pretty good. I did spray my face with a bit of water and blotted with a tissue. That really smoothed the areas that we’re looking a bit dry. I need to swap to a heavier winter moisturizer and and had done no skin prep prior to application. Given that I can’t judge this too harshly.  As to the shade, it’s not prefect but close. I wear Cream in Hourglass Vanish foundation. I think that makes me close to NW15-20 in MAC. I feel like the cool tone version of 21 would work better, but this one is neutral enough I can make it work. A lot of times neutrals lean too warm but this one doesn’t seem too which means it’ll work for more people. I think depth wise it’s okay, but If you’re at all darker than me get the next shade up.  At under $13 this is pretty incredible. It doesn’t come with a refill, but given the price I’m not going to complain. Please note if you’re buying this only for the compact my AmorePacific cushion doesn’t not fit in this at all. So if you use anything shaped like that it won’t work. You could just swap the sponge with the actual product though. I will for sure be keeping this case, my kids love it too!  In the photo I’m also wearing Hourglass AL powder in Etherial Light, blush in Luminous Flush (also on eyes), and lip gloss in Cosmic Pink

review: Much more than just hyaluronic acid! Very moisturizing and best fitting for my face. 5 stars⭐. I love these masks! For the price and how many you get, I was surprised to find the plastic backing. I really like this, because I can open it up and make a few cuts using the plastic and its cutouts as my guide to make it easier. I cut right through the plastic and the mask at the same time. I always have to cut a little slit at both the inner and outer corners of the eye openings, and also the outer corners of the mouth opening, as I like to move my mouth a bit and I have extremely dry eyes and the serum always gets into them, if I don't. This also lets it lay down flat on my nose and eyebrows better. I also cut four slits at about 10 and 2 o clock and 4:30 and 7:30, or roughly equal spacing coming upward diagonally from my eyes and coming down and outwards diagonally from the corners of my mouth. My face is a bit small, and this helps me to be able to overlap those areas and make them fit better, especially with larger masks. With these, I have to do the shallowest cutting ever, because they fit so well. They cover my entire face better than any mask I've used. I haven't had a problem with them lifting up or drying out at all. It also helps with something I will share later in my review. It takes a little finagling, but I manage to squeeze a bit of the serum off the mask while removing it from the package. I start before I even open the package by pushing all the serum to the bottom. I cut the top open, grab the top of the Mask, and fold the sides of the package inward, almost in half, using my non-dominant hand. I start pulling out the mask while squeezing the top closed around it as best I can. This squeezes out a good bit of the way too much extra serum that comes out if I don't do this. I love hyaluronic acid, but these masks have so many more wonderful ingredients than just that. Almost every ingredient is so nutrient-rich or moisturizing for the skin. I use Retin-A and these are the most soothing masks 1 to 2 days after my application nights, which are every 3 nights. These moisturize my face so well and they feel great while I have them on. I don't want to take them off when the timer goes off. There's plenty of serum in the package to use elsewhere, like on your neck & decollete, and even on your hands. I always put a moisturizer on afterwards to hold all the nutrients and moisture in properly. I learned a trick while back from another reviewer that I've been doing since I read it. When taking a mask off my face, I cut it into 4 pieces. Mainly, I cut them apart at the forehead, cheeks, and chin areas, using the four diagonal cuts I made, but you can make the cuts as you wish. I usually discard the small pieces that cover the nose and upper lip. I then take those four pieces, put them back in the serum that's left in the package remoisten them, with these that is no problem, or just add a little hyaluronic acid serum to moisten them again, put them on my neck and decollete area the best I can, and wait another 15 or 20 minutes. This really lets me get the most possible use out of every mask. I really love these masks and all of the skin loving ingredients they contain. They make my face feel wonderful afterwards and the effects last all day, if not longer. These are definitely on my must-have list. Highly recommend!

review: Good value if you’re not too picky about make-up brushes. Look...you can’t buy a set of 32 brushes for $7 and expect to receive a super high-end product. However, these brushes are perfectly usable. The bristles on some of the brushes remind a little bit of what you find with craft brushes, but they are soft and fairly dense and they do a decent job. I bought this set for my daughter because she does stage make-up for the students in her high school plays, and let’s be honest...the price is right for this type of use. There are enough brushes that she can still have plenty of clean brushes to use while someone washes the brushes she used on the previous student. She said the brushes apply product well enough that she has no complaints and they do wash up well. They haven’t lost any bristles after some very hard use and multiple washes so they get an A rating for durability. You can see from my photo that these brushes have been used a ton already, but they’re still going strong. The handles are just long enough to be comfortable to use and they feel sturdy. The handles don’t wiggle inside of the metal ferrules; they appear to be very securely attached. There is a great selection of brushes as well as duplicates of the most often used types so it’s a well-rounded set. They also come in a great roll-up case that makes them very portable and storage is a snap. These brushes may or may not be for you. If you’re picky about your makeup brushes then you probably won’t be satisfied with these because they just don’t have as nice of an appearance as more high-end brushes and the bristles aren’t as satiny soft and smooth as more expensive brushes. You’ll need to spend a little more to find what you’re looking for if you fall in this category (not much more, though...check my reviews for other awesome sets). However, if you’re looking for a good, usable and durable set for a teenager, if you’re a makeup novice and you’re just want something to learn with, etc., these brushes work perfectly well for their intended purpose. Overall, I recommend this brush set if you want a whole bunch of durable, usable brushes and you have reasonable expectations of the quality of the bristles based on the price of the set (in other words, don’t be expecting gold for the price of copper).  **Note - If my review has been helpful to you, click on the button below and let me know!**

review: Work as promised. I love these types of curls. They don't last a super long time, just 24 hours or less, but that's enough for me. **Tip I learned from someone else's review: take out the fasteners before rolling up each curl. Then, once it's rolled up tight, insert the fastener and close it. Do the same in reverse when you're ready to take the curlers out. Take out the fastener, then unroll your hair.** You'll find that your hair will not get stuck or pulled out like it would have if you tried to roll and unroll your hair with the fastener still inside the roller. Another tip: don't wrap the hair too tightly around the curler. keep it loose enough so that the curler is not squished flat. That way you'll actually be able to put in and take out the fastener. Plus, your hair will dry faster if it was wet before curling

review: Fantastic facial cleansing brush with some clear advantages over its competitors. I'm not new to the world of facial cleansing brushes.  I'm a firm believer in the wonders they can do for your skin, but going into trying this one I wasn't convinced that it could really be much better/different than what I'd already been using.  It seemed to me that one was pretty much like all the others, but boy was I wrong!  From the minute I opened this I knew I was getting something of a higher quality just in the way it was packaged with a helpful pared down instruction panel right on the inner portion of the box (versus the more in-depth and tedious instructions one finds in full booklets, though one is included with this as well) which then opens to the brush along with it's complimentary travel case in a gift quality presentation.  All of those were nice little details but what's most impressive comes down to the functionality, so here are the ways it's better than the cleansing brushes I'd been using:  (a) You can actually get this thing wet, go figure!  No, we're not talking full-on immersion but believe it or not a surprising number of cleansing brushes on the market will warn against water like it's acid, even advising you not to put water directly on the brush.  That's hard to do and for an object that's sole purpose is washing that was always a very disconcerting warning.  There are no worries with this one and it's much easier just wetting the brush and applying facial cleanser directly onto it rather than onto your skin and trying to quickly grab the brush before it all goes sliding off your face.  (b) The inclusion of a timer is wonderful.  The brush will give a slight pause alerting you to move on to the next region of your face (which is also highlighted in the picture instructions).  Making sure you give equal time to every portion of your face couldn't be simpler, and I think my favorite of all is that once you've finished the third zone the brush shuts itself off automatically, making sure you don't over-exfoliate.  It takes all the guess work out of it.  (c) I love that you get three different brush heads.  The skin on my cheeks tends to be more sensitive and can peel so I thought going in that I might have to use the sensitive brush but the regular brush has been just fine.  The bristles are softer than other brushes I've used but I don't think that's a bad thing.  I'm still seeing results and this brush actually feels much better on your face versus some others that are rough enough to leave your skin feeling sore afterwards.  I wasn't sure if the massaging brush head had any meaningful purpose to it in terms of skin health, but another reviewer suggested using it right after the cleansing and I think that's a fabulous idea.  It's like a nice little 2-step spa treatment.  (d) The ergonomic shape of the brush fits much more comfortably in my hand and the smaller overall size of the brush not only makes it great for traveling but allows you to more precisely get into every avenue of your face (like the bridge of the nose or between the nose and mouth) where larger brushes simply cannot go.  (e) The charger itself is conveniently small, a charge lasts a long time, and it has cool UFO looking lights that flash in a circular pattern around the brush head to alert you to when charging is ongoing and when it has stopped, again, taking the guess work out of it and also just being fun!

review: Works and makes buying jewelry less of a guessing game. I just recently found out I have a Nickel allergy. I just whip this little test kit out of my purse and swab the jewelry before I commit to buying it.  The solutions fit into the provided prescription style bottle, along with a few Q-Tip cotton swabs (which you have to provide).  All you do is put 2 drops of Solution A and 2 drops of Solution B on the tip of a swab and wipe it across the metal for several seconds. Whether this serum has actual anti-aging effects is questionable. My wrinkles haven't gone away at all. review: Hands down best quality for the price point.  No brassiness. 1B to 8ash & 22 medium blonde. I buy clip-in hair to add color depth and a little bit of drama, so this is not a review to add length.  This hair is perfect to blend in with fine hair or hair that is smooth (looks like you can use right out of the package). The hair has healthy "bounce" or body.  This is a review of 1B/8A/22 (dark black going to 8ash with 22 medium blonde mix)  This hair provides hard to achieve drama, going from deep dark brown/black to a lighter shade, without ANY brassiness.  This is nearly impossible to achieve on real hair (without ruining the cuticle), yet they did it and the hair appears HEALTHY.  The hair also appears relatively thick on the ends, unlike another recent purchase I made.  NOTE: Sadly, I might be returning this, so I did not disassemble the hair pieces from the package or even try these on (because another reader might receive my return).  Right now, I'm undecided.  Defining color over the internet is difficult  The ends are supposed to be #22 with 8A.  In the picture, it looks like a light blonde of 8.5 or even maybe a 9.  I decided to roll the dice in hopes that the picture would be more accurate than the description.  Upon receipt, this is a medium blonde that even leans a bit dark blonde...perhaps a level 7.5 at the lightest last few inches.  My natural hair color is a medium brown and I bleach it to a level 9.5.  Uniformly bleached hair, especially right after a root touch-up can make the face look washed out.  So this would have been perfect to add some interest and depth except I fear that the medium blonde-dark blonde will detract from the nearly platinum hair that I've worked hard to achieve.  This color is versatile and would be great for someone with medium blonde hair or any shade *darker*.  Unfortunately, for someone with level 9 or above, probably best to shop for a level 9 or 10 ombre.  Bummer, I really think this is gorgeous hair but it will not work for me

review: Overlooked and underrated. Turkish razors have been a barbers staple since disposable blades. Nearly every barber straight razor hot shave Ive had (before the ban on reusable blades), Sedef made an appearance for certain tasks. This should tell you something. I have no trust in reviews that obviously have no knowledge of the product type or experience with said "thing" prior to purchase. I have my great grandfather's straight razor. I can hone for shaving or woodcarving. I have lathered and shaved with a dozen knives. A few old timers may remember some of the DE blades in my picture, some are NA NOS and older than half the readers here, all are part of my rotation and stash. have used a half dozen straight edges. I have used all the general styles of shavette. I have EIGHT razors of this turkish style. Two sedef and six Ali Biyikli (identical except for name in same location, they may come from same factory for english and turkish markets for all I know). Why so many? Because they are cheap, thin for travel, the easiest to index your angles; be that your blade angle in a pinch grip, or just feeling where the blade is by the straight shank. The turkish is my favorite. It may look cheap, it may be cheap, but it is a great shave and due to its thin flat design, they get into tight spots more easily than any other shavette or straight razor. Do you get the picture that I did not just unbox my first shavette and try it a few times? Loading blades is super easy, and if someone says dangerous, they must be using the wrong methods to get blades in or out. These are meant for half DE blades, which can also be found already halved, as shavettes have been standardized for a long time. This review is long enough, you can find a video on how to if you cant figure it out without putting your fingers somewhere dangerous (this includes premeditating a slip and the resulting unintended motions to follow, much like carving or cutting). I have found sedef not only better in feel, as flat straight and thin is very easy to index. But it also very versatile. I have managed to run all kinds of blades. Some require modification to the blade; some to the razor holder... This i WILL explain but the pictures really should be self explanatory if you know what you are doing. I have never received one with a loose hinge, as they have a rubbery plastic spacer for friction. However i have had some loosen up over the years. But had no problem peening it with a light tap, or with vise grips and a light pinch. However with propper use, a loose handle is a non issue since it is always held in its position by your hand positioning. I no longer tighen a worn out one, as it makes it easy to switch positions and corresponding grip one handed. Much like a butterfly/ balisong. If you have used one, you know that you NEVER grab or use it by the handle (shavette or straight). You hold the tang only, and the handle is simply a blade cover you cannot lose because its attached. When they get loose, i leave it that way for ease of one handed use, and simply lock it closed for travel by slipping an O-ring over the smaller end. This is mostly so it doesnt open in a roughly treated bag and lever the plastic handle in a way that will break it. INJECTOR BLADES- the friction fit will hold it while shaving. However it does not fully seat, making it (actually) dangerous to load and adjust exposure. It will have no exposure and be stuck inside holder if you try to seat it fully. The solution is a shim to raise exposure height. I dedicated one razor to injectors. It has a metal shim. My primary is a stainless piece, but you may have troue finding the right size... So put a used (injector)  blade in a vise leaving an even reveal and file or dremmel the exposed part away. Now you have a shim. I am away from home writing this but made a quickie from wood that shows better on camera anyway. Hence the small travel kit in pic (sedef, blades, diy folding brush, alum and tabac in a chapstick tube fits in a sunglasses case. If the picture does not make it obviously clear what to shim my words may be no help. Those who get it, may see why I like these. Injector blades are great if you have thick wire hairs or want better longevity. I also run Personna "hair shaper blades" (the 2.5" type shown) the other hair shaper types can be used too but may require a shim as described above. All you need for this style is how to safely de-spine a single edge blade,as picture shows half removed. My method is not shown on youtube but should be, as i have found safer easier ways than the end nippers.. But point being that its quite simple, and then you simply install the blade. review: This is a good set of contouring colors. This is a good set of contouring colors.  It has a huge range of colors needed for dark skin, to light skin, It even includes a white cream for highlighting along with some green and pinks to even out skin tone.  Basically this set is a great set to start with and to have on hand for when your skin goes thru some funky changes.  We all have that happen from time to time.  Anyways my contouring kit is a cream set of 15 colors.  Each color is very creamy and I had no issues with blending and rubbing in.  However I always use a high quality primer with all makeup so that may add to the easy technique of blending into the mixture.  Each color has its advantages along with its disadvantages.  Like I said not every color is going to suit your needs so If you are looking for specific colors this is not the set for you, this is a range of colors for different shades of skin. The makeup seemed to be long wearing but please dont forget that I used primer and that could have something to do with makeup wear length.  I also did not break out with this cream as I have done with so many other colors.  Of course I made sure to clean my face off each evening and I never slept in it at all.  The plastic holding the makeup tins is a hard black plastic,  I wouldnt call it super high quality but its not the cheapest I have come across.  The reason for 4 stars is because I prefer mirrors in the compact as sometimes I like to have my makeup in hand while applying and it would be nice if a mirror was included.  However it takes no value away from the makeup its just my personal preference.  I also need to research some of these ingredients,  (which I havent done as of yet while writing the review)  I have not recongized a couple and usually most ingredients I am somewhat familiar with as I am a makeup fanatic.  Nothing jumps out and screams do not put on your face though.  I also wish the ingredients was listed on the hard plastic case so once you dispose of the box which everyone does you still have a list of ingredients in case you have some delayed reaction after long term use.  Another reason for 4 stars.  However overall I am pleased with this makeup palette.  It seems to be well suited for a starter pack for those learning to contour, and those whose skin goes thru some weird skin tones from time to time.  My only complaints were the ones listed above and no others.  Makeup seems to spread smoothly and blends well.  Which is what most women prefer when it comes to contouring.  I did notice it did take several coats and more during application than what I am used to however compared to regular drug store kits its pretty comparable to it, may be a tad better in quality as it blends easily. I received this makeup palette for free for testing and reviewing purposes,  I have come to this conclusion by using and wearing this makeup for a few days myself

review: Cute? Yes. Self-adhering? Only sort of. Finicky packaging? Yes.. So I have to say that these lashes are cute, light, have a great shape to them and blend with my natural lash well. They have a great texture to them, are made well, and I feel like I'll get a lot of wear out of them. BUT, saying that the lashes fully self-adhere is... only sort of right. Do they stick to you on their own? Yes. Will they last like that all day? Maybe, maybe not. Probably not. Every time I've worn these, I've used a dot of lash glue to keep them stuck down on the inside edges of my lid, because otherwise they're very willing to peel off. Once they start peeling, they won't stop. That's how lashes work. So, a little bit of glue, and I'm good. But, then we get to an issue. The included adhesive is a little thick - thicker than a layer of glue, for sure. Now that I'm whipping the glue out anyway, I wouldn't have minded gluing the lash on. And, more importantly, BECAUSE OF THE THICKNESS OF THE ADHESIVE, these do not sit as close to your lash (as easily) as a pair of glue lashes. Period. There is more of a gap to fill between your actual lash and this lash because they won't comingle like they would if the adhesive was thinner. Lastly, getting them out of their packaging is weird. Each lash is on a "tower" with a "lid", and the "towers" are on a tray. When you try to remove the "lid" from either "tower," you'll realize that the "tower" comes off of the tray - you then have a very small little plastic block with an even smaller (and thinner) plastic lid keeping the lash on. Finicky. Weird.  Overall they look cute on me, and they are priced fairly. In the future, I might just use them with glue, though

review: As Advertised- Really nice salon-quality face smoothing treatment. I have been seeing these kind of moisture/calming masks on some of the morning talk shows so decided to try Yew Tree Stem Cell Perfect Calming Soothing Mask.  Korean beauty is hot right and needed to try as I LOVE finding new beauty products.  Most plant stem cell beauty products use the  Edelweiss, a mountain flower so Yew Tree a stem cell product from the Yew Tree is intriguing.  They come wrapped in 5 individual packages with full description and directions on each.  I started with a freshly cleansed face and added the very wet mask to my face.  Took a little finagling to get it in place but once I did, it stayed in place.  The strip that goes above the lip could be a bit wider, as that is a spot that could use some smoothing for some women, but all the rest is pretty "face friendly".  I let it sit for 20 minutes, rinse with cool water and was pleasantly surprised at how fresh my face looked.  No need for any additional moisturizer.  I dabbed a little eye cream under my eyes and was good to go.  Also, as to not let a drop of the soothing elixir that is leftover in the package and fingers, I smooth it over my neck and decolletage.  Very nice!  I am in my early 50's and it really is nice to look fresh and dewy-skinned, even if it is just a temporary home beauty treatment.  Huge splurge for me but if you went to a salon, it would cost you a whole lot more.  A luxurious splurge that makes your face look, and feel special.  A friend is getting married this Spring and can't afford expensive salon treatments, so I am putting a special spa bag together for her and a couple single packages of Yew Tree Stem Cell Perfect Calming Soothing Mask will be front and center in her "home" salon treatment pack.  I am pleased with this product.  I almost took a star away for the too thin strip for the above lip area but that could just be me being cranky.  Seemed like a lot of care and research went into making it and it shows

review: Very close and comfortable shave. I'm almost 50 and have been using an electric razor most of my shaving life. When my trusty Norelco needed replacing, my wife bought me the latest self-cleaning Braun for a Christmas gift. I liked some aspects of it, but it always had a hard time shaving my neck area without going back over it a lot of times. Replacing the cutter and screen every 6 months or so helped keep it from getting progressively worse, but after a couple of years, I thought I would try something different.  I read MANY reviews and decided to try the Norelco Spectra system. I've been using it for several months now and I can tell you the difference on my neck is like night and day. The Norelco is MUCH faster and smoother than the Braun and cuts very close after only a couple of passes. I was amazed at how much better it was than even my old triple-head Norelco.  If I were to have ANY negative, it would be the charging system. The first problem is, if you provide a recharging "stand", then the logic (IMO) should be that the stand be allowed to be plugged in 24/7 with the razor in it, without any adverse affects. However, MANY places in the manual tell you DOING THIS WILL SHORTEN THE LIFE OF YOUR BATTERY.  Because they use a NiCad battery, they ask that you only recharge it when it runs low to avoid the "memory" effect and associated diminished capacity. I can understand that, but the second problem is, it gets fully charged in only 4 hours! After that, you are supposed to remove it from, or unplug, the stand to avoid overcharging. Unfortunately, most of us shave in the morning before a work day, then don't return for at least 9-10 hours. In my case, a 12 or even 24 hour charge would be far more convenient. What's so hot about a "4-hour charge" anyway?? OK, how about I push a button to start the charge cycle, and it automatically shuts off when fully charged! How easy is that? (Gee, that's exactly how my Braun worked.)  Being an Electrical Engineer myself, I'm sometimes overly critical of things like this. OK, if it were me, (are you listening Norelco???) I would have used a NiMH battery that didn't have to be "deep cycled", then use a lower current "trickle charge" base that could be left on 24/7. A side benefit is when you pack for a trip and grab your razor, you KNOW it's always 100% charged and will probably have enough juice to last the entire trip without dragging the charger along.  OK, maybe the charger is not as bad as I make it out to be. I just think it could be better. I give it 3 stars, while the razor itself gets a full 5 stars

review: Perfect Placing Stamper! (updated). The clear stamper came just as described. I haven't actually used it on my nails yet but I have played around with it on some paper and it picks up the images perfectly. After reading some concerning reviews on other clear stampers I was hesitant to purchase this one. However, I have had no problems as of yet. The only flaw is that there are two little dent/scratches on the stamper head and I am afraid eventually it will lead to bigger dents/scratches. With it being so inexpensive I wouldn't mind purchasing another one for back-up, just in case. I do not use any scrapers that come with the stampers, as I use gift cards because they are much easier to use and swipe with.  The stamper head is squishy but not marshmallow squishy. It is possible to squish on your nail without rolling, so long as you do not have extremely wide nail beds. It is a little hard to get used to being able to see through and it takes some practice getting it lined up exactly where you want, but it's easier once you do it a few times. As I stated earlier, the images are very crisp and clean when being picked up. Instead of squishing down like I did with my other stamper I instead try to roll/flick the stamper across. This is more for the fear of damaging the stamper, as I've read about others who did not have success with clear stampers.  Make sure that when you use it you do not clean it with acetone/polish remover as it will eventually make the stamper head cloudy and no longer see through. Also, do not buff or anything before first use, I found that it picks up perfectly without having to do any of that.  I highly recommend getting this stamper if you love to stamp but have problems with perfect placing, such as myself.  *****UPDATE******  I have no idea what happened but I've recently been trying to use this stamper and it will just not work. I've used so many different polishes, different brands and nothing! I had no problem at all and picked up images very well, however now it picks up less than half of the image which is extremely frustrating. I spent about 2 hours this morning doing all kinds of different things, using different polishes, using different techniques, different stamping plates and nothing is working! I've tried priming it like you would a non-clear stamper which includes wiping the head with acetone and buffing it with a file

review: Best Peeling Kit I've Tried So Far. This is the 3rd peel foot mask that I have tried. The others have been unsuccessful. Still wanting to experience the foot peel, I tried again. The first thing that makes this foot peel better than the others is the foot slippers. The slippers are actually a medium thickness plastic. They remind me of the “rubber pants” that my little boy wore over his training underwear when he was 2 years old. These slippers also fit the best of the three that I have tried. I had problems with using the tape, but because my feet are on the larger end, they stayed in place well without it. I wear a size 10 W shoe and these fit my feet fine. They were not too tight nor did I have to stretch them to get them on. They were a little confusing to figure out. The directions said to “cut on the dotted line” but I couldn’t see any dotted line. The 2 slippers were attached together at the top. So I cut them apart and then I had to snip a little off the top to open up where my foot was to go inside. This foot peel has a somewhat pleasant scent. I was worried because one of the ingredients is vinegar and another is fermented milk. Those did not sound appealing at all. However, what I smelled was a combination of the ginger and the chamomile. The hardest thing about this whole process was carving out the time to do it. You have to soak your feet for 15-30 minutes before hand. Then you have to wear the foot booties for 70-90 minutes. Then soak for another 15 minutes afterwards. I’m a busy mom, so it’s hard to find that much free time. I've just started noticing some peeling, so already it's looking more successful than the other ones that I've tried.  *I purchased these at a discounted price in exchange for my honest & unbiased review. My thoughts & opinions are my own

review: nice formula, feels good, absorbs well, effective. This is my 2nd container. Love GoMay. I have used this before! I had used several GoMay products about a two years ago. I have liked them all, and there are some products that I have repurchased (love their aminos face wash). I remember really liking this night cream, and so when it came up as an option to try, I thought maybe it was another version, but no it is the same. I think the change has been in the company. They were entirely a Chinese brand, and now I see USA labeling- but I think it is still a Chinese beauty product. Same stuff that I know and love. Same press down dispenser container. I am copying over my old review as the info is all the same, and my experience is the same. While I dont rate on price, I am pleased at its effectiveness and how it is half the price of similar items I have used.  Safe, effective moisturizing product with promising ingredients. I am used to using several of these ingredients, and I must stress that it is important to use SPF when using anything with retinol. I saw that this has quite a list of ingredients that I am not totally familiar with, so I went through each one and looked them up. I included a short description of each (and included EWG rating for those that like that sort of information). You will note that most all have a very GOOD rating of 1 or 2. The only ingredient that has a higher number (bad) is for the retinol- and that is because of the degree to which retinol/vitamin A, by nature can absorb into the skin (toxicity) and how our skin is more sensitive to UV rays. So again, wear your SPF when using any retinol based products.  --GoMay is a Chinese (turned USA) beauty company and from everything I have used, the products have been impressive in formulation and the thought and safety put into creating it.  --Awesome, attractive container. Has a press down lid that pops out some product. Keeps it clean and safe! BUT if you want to get into the container, the lid does come off.  --Minimal scent- naturally occurring. review: Very good for giving texture and body to heavy, thick hair. I have tried all kinds of mousses, hair sprays, gels, you name it, to provide some texture and hold for my very thick, somewhat frizzy hair.  Left to itself, my hair frizzes up into a kind of nondescript limp mess if just left to air dry.  When blown dry, it looks good for half an hour and then it just flattens to my head, limp and without any shape.  No amount of hair spray, mousse or gel has both given my hair texture AND kept it in place and natural-looking for more than an hour.  This Exotic Argan Oil Texture Paste is very good at providing texture to my hair without looking greasy or leaving flakes or film.  It is definitely the best thing I have ever used, and I am in my 50's and I think I've used everything out there.  One complaint I have though , I have to add several layers of it - first I dip my fingers in several times, getting enough to kind of coat the ends of my fingers, and then I run my fingers through my wet hair; then I blow it dry and again dip my fingers in several times to rub it all over the ends (to keep them separated and give them some body) and then I rub it through the fine hairs that stick up on top of my head.  So this is quite the procedure, but in the end I am pretty happy with the result.  It keeps its shape and is more textured than with any other product.  That said, I still have to spray hairspray all over to keep the style and "bounciness" from falling out.  So I am giving it four stars because I wish I could just slap on a little of this and go. review: ERSATZ PRODUCT, NOT AUTHENTIC. I normally buy Renpure shampoo at Whole Foods and absolutely love it. If you see this product in store, definitely get it - it's a great shampoo, but DO NOT buy this on Amazon. I am not sure what is in the bottle I received, but I know for sure it is NOT the real product. I still had 1/3 of the store bought bottle left when this new bottle from Amazon arrived so I was able to compare the 2 products.  1. Color - The bottle from Amazon is significantly darker than the real stuff. I certainly do not think an authentic bottle of Renpure would be produced in a revolting shade of yellow akin to urine from an underhydrated person. Off-putting for sure.  2. Scent - Why would I willingly smell a bottle of urine colored liquid? I don't know. I've been quarantined for weeks and was feeling brave and bored. The smell, thankfully, was not that of putrid urine, but that of a sweaty sock stewed in mud. While it is undoubtedly thought-provoking that a product meant to cleanse you actually smells like it will do the exact opposite, the juxtaposition of function and scent is not what I look for in a shampoo.  3.  Texture. It is much thicker than the real product. Not sure what additional chemicals were mixed in to achieve the gelatinous texture, but it resulted in a lot more suds, which dried out my scalp. Thanks to the grimy residue and moisture-stripping effects of this knock off shampoo, my shoulders would have you fooled that is has been snowing in April - the dandruff flakes are large and they are real. Real Renpure shampoo does NOT do this.  4. Safety. I guess the joke is on me because the bottle did not come with a seal top. This bottle was definitely tampered with and I was the idiot who risked it and put it on my hair. Don't make the same mistake.  I am extremely disappointed in Amazon for selling me a bottle of inferior product. I will NOT be buying this again. It looks like pee and leaves your hair smelling and feeling dirtier than it did before you washed it. Do yourself a favor and buy this in stores instead, that way you know it's real

review: Truly some wonderful stuff to fight "winter hands". I hate winter for a lot of reasons, but one of them is that my hands get so dry that I get cracks at my fingertips. It’s annoying and painful, especially at night. I’ve tried all sorts of moisturizers without much success. The best results (if you can call it that) have been from using petroleum jelly, but that’s messy and it still doesn’t work well.  This argan oil, however, has been hugely effective. It gave me results right from the first day, and over the course of just a few days I can see noticeable healing of the skin cracks. No more pain and my hands feel far better than any other treatment I’ve tried.  The product comes very nicely packaged, with a nice box filled with shredded packing material to keep the glass bottle safe in transit. It also makes for a very nice presentation should you want to give this as a gift. The bottle comes with a dropper and a “spritz” head. The latter is my only quibble – the spray head didn’t work well at all, and made sort of a mess when using it to dispense the oil. I replaced it with the dropper and had much better results.  The oil itself has little or no scent. You need very, very little for results – I use about 1-2 small drops per hand, and that’s more than enough. It spreads easily (as expected given that it’s oil). It does take a few minutes to soak in – my hands are very greasy when I first apply it, but after a few minutes the greasiness goes away. The sheen from the oil stays around longer, but that too dissipates after 30 minutes or so.  This can be used for a wide range of applications including face, body and even hair. It comes with a good amount of information to help explain how/where to use it, and how the oil was processed.  I’m very impressed with this oil – it’s the only product I’ve ever tried that totally worked to solve my dry/cracked hands. It’s not cheap, but well worth the price if you need a highly effective moisturizer. Highly recommend. [Sample provided for review]

review: A beautiful assortment of rainbow colors in a variety of finishes! 🌈 Stellar formula!. If you're looking to build your gel polish collection on a budget, this set of 20 colors from Rosegin has you covered. There's a little bit of everything in this kit - crèmes, full coverage microglitters, jellies, and crelly finishes. They also include a base, as well as glossy and matte no-wipe topcoats (both of which are phenomenal!) The glossy top is super shiny and the matte top looks like velvet.  Rosegin curated a lovely rainbow assortment of mini gel colors in this set. You get pastels and primary colors, but no black or white polish is included. The bottles are 5ml; though they look tiny, they're filled to the top and contain enough product for several mani's. I swatched 12 out of the 20 shades in this kit and the formulas are amazing! Smooth and buttery. Beautifully pigmented - 2 coats to full coverage. The glitters aren't thick or clumpy, and don't leave bald spots during application. review: weightless, non tacky, fully absorbs quickly, NO added fragrance, no scent. I have Rosacea, specifically type 1 where I experience redness from flushing and visible veins (telangiectasias). Otherwise clear skin. While topicals won't really help the veins, I can use products that help even out skin tone where it is pink from flushing. Some products can initially make my skin red, then it calms down (especially if new). This ISNTREE Cica Relief Ampoule Duo Set has not irritated my skin. In fact, it has helped to minimize aggravated skin.  The serum is extremely light. I think the lightest weight product I have ever used. The bottles are small, and I feel like I am going through it quickly. I may be using too much, I dont know. I  do apply to neck and chest as well as face. I already use a product with EGF (epidermal growth factor), and I thought that maybe in serum form it would feel like a more concentrated dose. I have no idea how much Isntree uses, but this product feels like the emphasis is on the Centella Asiatica Extract. That isn't necessarily a bad thing, I am just not sure yet what I think about the performance of this product for my skin.  The two small bottles would be better as 1 bottle.  --super light weight --absorbs instantly --not tacky --skin feels instantly smooth (I also use some on the back of my hands) --I wouldn't use it alone as a moisturizer, especially if have dry skin (like me) --gentle, doesn't aggravate my skin, but that very well could differ for everyone (esp those w/ damaged skin barrier) --contains soothing centella asiatica extract --contains EGF- worth doing some research to see the benefits and to discount myths. --ingredients that can help build and maintain skin barrier. Especially important for those with skin conditions where they are exacerbated by a damaged skin barrier. Got super sensitive skin? work on repairing that skin barrier before anything else. --NO added fragrance in ingredient list. No naturally occurring scent either. I cant detect any aroma.  My skin: mid 40s, smooth and clear (except for visible veins), leans dry. I follow this up with a moisturizing SPF (their sunscreens are great) or a moisturizer if using at night.  I dont think it is bad. I really just think it is ok. I would give it 3.5 stars if I could. For me it isn't quite a 4 star product, so I am going with the middle of the road rating of 3. Your experience will vary. I think it would be especially appealing to those who prefer a weightless non tacky Centella Asiatica product. While I have zero issues with this, I am not likely to repurchase it. I have preferred products, especially for EGFs. However, if I notice anything else-- good or bad, I will be sure to update. It can take at least 2 weeks for a product to show its effectiveness, and it can take that long for the skin to acclimate to a new product. I am a little early on writing this, but my skin is used to centella asiatica as well as EGFs, and with some Isntree products

review: Pretty natural looking. Finally, after over a year of having these, I actually tried them out! I’ve never worn false lashes before and was hesitant to use them (obviously since I’ve had them a year without using them - lol!). I used a magnifying makeup mirror though and did fine. The photos of the eyelash after it was applied was my first attempt ever to do this so it’s definitely not perfect but it was much easier to apply than I expected it to be. I am sure my results will improve with practice. These are secured in place with magnetic eyeliner (I guess I am pretty ignorant about these things but I had never heard of that!). The eyeliner goes on smoothly; actually better than some liquid eyeliner that I’ve used in the past. It’s a little tricky to get them in the best spot. Like I said previously though, I think this will get much easier the more times I try them. It comes with tweezers to use but it was almost easier for me to apply them without using them. I didn’t wear them long. I will have to get used to how they feel; it wasn’t uncomfortable, just different for me. I have very thin, light-colored eyelashes so I think I’m really going to enjoy these! review: Like a Peach Bellini for your Face!. Do you like champagne cocktails? This one smells like a combination of peach and champagne, and even looks like it! It comes out like a gel. It's activated by water, so after washing your face, leave your face damp and put a thin layer of the gel quickly all over your face. Include your neck if you like. Then with each passing moment, it's going to get foamier and foamier. That's why you have to have a very thin coat. You only need a small amount of product. If you use too much, your face is going to foam up like you have shaving cream all over!  After about 5 or 10 minutes, you massage a little bit with warm water and then rinse. After you dry your face it's going to feel squeaky clean. If you have dry skin, you're ready for a moisturizing serum and cream. If you have oily or acne prone skin, use the appropriate products for that skin type. I don't feel that this mask is drying, but it does leave you very clean.  So, in my opinion, this is good for all skin types, as long as you use it as a brightening mask as opposed to a hydrating mask. This is just what your skin needs if you have overdosed on hot humid weather.please look at the ingredients to see if you have any sort of allergy or if any of them are a trigger for any skin issues. Because I have sensitive skin that can be triggered, but I only left it on for about 4 minutes. I had absolutely no irritation, but I think if I had left it on longer, I might have. That doesn't mean it's bad for you. If you leave a mild castile soap, which is so gentle, on your face for any length of time, skin will be irritated. Made in the USA, from Tonica Skin in Marblehead Massachusetts.  I hope this review has helped you to make a decision about whether or not you'd like to try this fun mask. It really does leave your skin feeling and looking energized, but it's a bit of an investment. Nice splurge for a spa night, and because the product comes out via a pump, it's going to be sanitary for all the participants. It's going to make for some really fun and Instagram worthy photos!  xxoo  PS, my 'spa night' pal doesn't look too impressed 😆

I was careful not to hold the trimmer by the click wheel to avoid accidentally going down a setting... I did that once and clicked from a 5 to a 4.  I liked the 4 better anyway, so stuck with that. review: Many probiotic side effects are due to release and growth too early in the gut.. Personal experience that may or may not be helpful.  If you have IBS, you may well have small intestinal bacterial overgrowth (SIBO).  In either case, taking a probiotic that is not enteric-coated or coated for release AFTER your small intestine may make your symptoms worse because you are recolonizing your small intestine (this includes Align, and most on the market).  This product is enteric-coated, so should release after the small intestines to avoid putting bugs in the wrong place.  Read product info carefully to confirm enteric-coated, since they have other products.  They also have liquid versions that will dump the bugs in your small intestine.  If you're microbiome is jacked up, BIG doses of any probiotic may mess you up.  I used the 12.5 billion version of this product (available elsewhere) to avoid over-doing it and it seemed OK for me, but maybe not you (see other review on backing off 25 billion).  Take home message is always start small.  Tread lightly.  If you react, this may be rapid growth in your small intestine with bloating.  If you react, you may be reacting to the prebiotics in the product, not the probiotic itself.  Avoid prebiotics initially if very sensitive.  These bacteria may release d-lactate (brain fog).  They may make you feel worse regardless particularly if you're sensitive to histamine in food, since these strains make histamine as a byproduct of normal metabolism.  Bifidobacteria may not do this to the same degree, but these again should be engineered for release later in the gut (maybe Pearls Adult 50+ or others).  Pearls Adult 50+ contain only bifidobacteria similar to those in Align.  Align dumps in your small intestine.  S. boulardii is a yeast and seems to be more tolerable (to me) that may help repair and get combat bad bacteria, but it will not of itself rebalance your bacteria

review: Great body wash for sensitive skin!. I have very fair, very sensitive skin that is prone to itching and rashes.  Most bars of soap (and by most I mean 99%) are too strong for my skin so I am on the constant lookout for a product that I can use as a shower gel.  I asked myself "Who else has sensitive skin besides me?"  BABIES!!!  So I turned to looking for products created for a baby's skin.  I detest the scent of lavender and for some reason most baby products contain lavender.  Yuck!  I read the reviews on the Sweet Baby Shampoo and saw that some folks recommended it also as a shower gel.  I'm a FANATICAL ingredient reader and I was pleased with the ingredients.  So, my first purchase was the Coconut Baby.  I liked what the product did for my skin as well as what it did not do.  It left my skin feeling soft and not irritated.  I loved the way it lathered, not too much but not too little.  It made a soft, creamy, bubbly lather.  I just wasn't crazy about the scent.  It has a faint plastic play-doh smell.  But then, to my nose most coconut scents end up smelling that way.  I was just hoping this would be different.  My next venture with Sweet Baby was with the vanilla scent.  The scent is a soft, buttery vanilla.  When I smell it, it makes me close my eyes and say "yum".  I haven't used it on my hair and I probably never will so I can't comment on it as a shampoo.  For now, this will be my staple shower gel.  By the way, I love the baby lotion as well!  I would definitely recommend both the shampoo as a shower gel and the lotion

review: Also great for dry, brittle, baby-fine, slippery hair!!!. While most of the reviews for these clips are to promote them for thicker hair, I am here to tell all of you who have hair like mine - dry, brittle, slightly kinky, fly-away, baby-fine, slippery - that these work great for our hair, too.  You know what kind of problems we have with clips and bands and what-not either falling out of our hair while trying to use them, or worse, pulling our hair out when we remove them.  I think this happens for two reasons:  One, our hairs are so fine that they actually get caught in the small tiny working parts of these kinds of clips - cracks that a thicker hair shaft is simply too large to get caught in. My sister's hair is the opposite of mine - dense, poker straight, and an extremely thick shaft - and she was surprised when I told her about this happening to me. It's hard to believe, but it happens to us all the time!!  In fact, I have to wind electrical tape onto new brushes where the handle meets the head because individual hairs get caught in the crack there all the time if I don't seal it up.  Let me tell you, OUCH. It took me years to figure that one out.  The other problem is that once treated with product and dried, and especially flat-ironed, baby-fine hair feels wonderful to the touch but it is very *slippery*.  If you use a roller or a clip that does not hold well or is too heavy, it simply falls out. Useless!  So... these are stronger & lighter, and the moving parts are better made, than any other ones I have tried of their kind.  And they work really well for my fickle, difficult hair.  I am not saying that these won't ever pull your hair out if you are careless and move too fast.  I am also not saying that they won't fall out if you don't secure them properly.  They will.  But if you have baby-fine hair then you have already learned to slow down and concentrate to avoid those problems anyway.  :)

review: Lightweight and Surprisingly Gentle on Acne Prone skin. Oz Naturals through Brandbacker provided me with this product for free to review. I was sent their SPF 30 Tinted Sunscreen Moisturizer in the shade medium. Oz Naturals claims that this product is safe for all skin types and can be worn alone as a foundation type product or under your makeup. I have combination oily acne prone skin so I was a bit nervous testing this out. I'm pleased to report I had no issues and did not break out any more than usual. When I first squeezed the tube of sunscreen, I was worried because of how dark the lotion seemed. I'm pretty fair in skin tone, and I really didn't want to look all streaky and "oompa loompa-ish." But to my surprise, this product blended out very nicely and easily. It gave me more of a healthier looking glow and it evened out my complexion, and had a very light but decent coverage over any redness on my face. This product smells to me a bit like baby wipes upon initial application, which I personally didn't mind, but it might be off-putting to some people more sensitive to scents. What I really loved most about this tinted sunscreen was how light it felt on my face. It didn't feel tacky or heavy, and dried down very quickly. I actually forgot I had it on at one point! Oz Naturals, like most sunscreens, recommends that this product be reapplied every two hours. This product retails for $21.99, which is pretty pricey in my opinion. However, it is a very good facial sunscreen that will mesh well with most skin types. I think if you haven't yet found your "holy grail" facial sunscreen, the Oz Naturals Sunscreen Moisturizer is worth trying out!

review: Tape In Extensions. I purchased the 18" and 22" tape in extensions (4P/27&2) and overall I am satisfied.  The color shown on-line was the color I received, it was extremely accurate, the hair seemed a little bit sparse at the ends but it was fine, my stylist said they felt good and went in smoothly.  My hair is pretty short but curling it all seems to help blend everything in.  This is the first time I tried the tape-in's and I do really like them, they are very easy to sleep in which was one of my main concerns.  Previously I had the microbeads and those drove me crazy.  I thought the price was fair and they offered a large variety of color options which was part of the reason I ended up with these.  I also did a lot of research before deciding on the tape-in's, it was helpful getting familiar with all the pro's and con's.  I also purchased extra tape and adhesive remover so I had it on-hand in case these started to come out.  So far I haven't had any pieces fall out or feel like they were loose and they seem easy to manage but I have only had these in less than a week and have only washed my hair once.  Here are some semi-negative things that I am keeping my eye on but when I curled my hair there were several times it left black stuff on my curling iron and I was under the impression if it was human hair it wouldn't do that, so we will see how things go.  The hair feels not as soft as I think it should so that bothers me a little bit especially since I have only had them in for such a short time.  The last thing I noticed is that some of the pieces of hair are almost picky/itchy, which I found to be weird.  I am not sure that I will purchase these again would like to try another brand so I have some better comparisons on which ones are best suited for me.  But overall I am pretty happy with these

review: Unique product, tastes good, and it works!. I know this candy is expensive, but it does what it says it will, which is a big deal for me.  This candy is actually sort of a life-changing product for me, and I'm so excited it's available in the US now.  I sweat easily and profusely.  It's an embarrassing problem, but this candy makes it much less so.  I shower and use underarm deodorant, obviously, which helps the situation there, but the rest of me sweats too... just a general moistness of the skin all over, which often has a somewhat sour smell.  Yuck.  I'm always the first one in any group to start to sweat if it's warm or we're doing something vigorous.  Usually this leaves me feeling really self-conscious and I will stand apart, etc.  I've even avoided certain activities with friends during the summer because I knew this would happen.  For this candy to help me, I just eat a few pieces an hour or two in advance! Then, when I start to get warm my skin will give off a subtle lovely smell instead of the usual sour smell.  I can't tell you how excited I am about this!  Also, a side bonus, it has a nice effect on the breath that lasts longer for me than any breath mint I've ever used.  Maybe it's just the way it reacts with my own body chemistry, but I don't think it smells particularly like roses, or even flowery... it's hard to explain, it's just a subtle clean & fresh smell that comes through my skin.  You know how some people just smell good, not like product, but just like a nice skin smell?  That's what this does for me.  A friend of mine ate some and I thought she smelled more flowery, more reminiscent of roses, though not quite.  I'd expect it's going to smell a little different on everyone.  Oh, and since it's a candy, I should probably mention:  It's delicious!  The very first taste when you pop it in your mouth is a little "rosey", meh, but that is almost immediately replaced by a very nice tangy tangerine flavor.  I have to keep myself from eating them all up so I'll have them when I need them.  :)  I buy the regular sugar-sweetened kind, since I don't use artificial sweeteners, so I can't comment on the taste of the sugar-free ones
